| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144066758/662289482/-224335339?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGRlZTEwOGItMmNlOS1mMTExLTkxZjMtMDAwZDNhNTMzMTliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KGH0Za1_k8IAhCPBjrvsWbiKJsT8t1nT8zhGFNntksE=) Hi friend, I wanted to send you a quick note to let you know how grateful I am for everything you do for our district, and everything you have just helped do for our Democracy. Whether you read our emails, donate, volunteer, or offer words of encouragement, your support for a better society truly means so much. This has been a rollercoaster first term, from the pessimism after Trump’s election to the horrors of the Los Angeles wildfires, to the resilience our communities showed for each other with each challenge, and now to the hope we feel after historic wins across the ballot. It is a gift to represent a country and district I love, and I know there is still so much to fight for. But today, I just want to reiterate how eternally thankful I am for the district I call home.
May you have a few days of solitude and joy with your loved ones. Thank you, friend, and Happy Thanksgiving. Laura

Dear Friend, I hope you and yours have a very Happy Thanksgiving! Below is some recent information about economic development and infrastructure dollars making their way to our district. I am proud to call Central Oregon home and am honored to continue representing you in Salem. Sincerely,
Vikki Breese Iverson
House District 59
* * *
# **Rep. Breese Iverson Highlights Nearly $4.6 Million in Industrial and Infrastructure Investments for House District 59**
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
** November 25, 2026 **PRINEVILLE, Ore.** — State Representative Vikki Breese Iverson (R-Prineville) today highlighted $4.6 million in state infrastructure and economic development investments secured for communities across House District 59 through the Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF) and Industrial Site Loan Fund (ISLF) programs. The investments include funding for water infrastructure in Terrebonne, transportation planning in Crook County, development planning in Madras, and industrial site expansion in Prineville. “I am intentional every time I go to Salem to make sure rural Oregon has a seat at the table. By working closely with local government, businesses, and community partners, we can connect our communities with key state resources needed to support infrastructure and economic development. These investments are a great example of what we can accomplish when we work together and advocate with a shared vision for our region,” said Rep. Breese Iverson. **Regional Infrastructure Fund Awards**
* Terrebonne Domestic Water District received $375,000 for the Terrebonne Water Main Replacement Project.
* Flat Rock Road District received $250,000 for the Special Road District Access Safety and Route Refinement Plan.
* City of Madras received $163,000 for the Madras Federal Land Release Planning Project.

**Industrial Site Loan Fund Award**
* The City of Prineville received $3.9 million through the Industrial Site Loan Fund for the Prineville Bulk Facility Expansion project.

I’m looking forward to spending some time with my family this week, but before I head to the kitchen to start cooking, I wanted to share a quick note. I’m so grateful for this beautiful state, for my wife and three amazing kids, and for the life we’ve built here together. And this year, despite all the challenges we've faced, I've found even more reasons to be grateful. From neighbors looking out for one another and communities organizing to protect their rights to voters turning out in record-setting numbers, I've seen people refuse to give up on each other. I’m grateful for the strength and resolve of Californians and Americans who continue to show up, speak out, and participate in our democracy. And though it may sound nerdy to say, I’m thankful for the law! Our Constitution was built for challenging moments — it was built to protect us from tyranny and abuses of power, and I am deeply grateful that I get to play a role in defending it every day. However you’re spending Thanksgiving, I hope you’re able to take a moment to reflect and to connect with loved ones. From my family to yours, happy Thanksgiving. —Rob Bonta

Happy early Thanksgiving, friends! This is Marilyn, and I am so thrilled to get to spend these days at home with the family. I'm thinking this year, maybe I'll even venture myself to help Lucas cook dinner (it is kind of his thing, but maybe we can mix it up this year!). While I don't take anything for granted and feel absolutely grateful for all the daily things we don't always think about, like being healthy, having a warm place to call home, or having a job. I also feel especially grateful because we can afford a meal and the time we get to spend with our loved ones.

I wanted to take this space to remind us all that this is not the case for every American. Just yesterday, in fact, I was chasing Harvey through the grocery store and caught Lucas in line with a mostly empty cart just ten minutes after we'd gotten there. I mean, I know Harvey was being a terror, but we hardly had anything! It turns out he was buying some food for someone who was clearly in a rough spot and needed the help. Yes, he really is that guy.
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.af3YsMHat2ywQZWWE1Zu4adRoN2vB_lW4B48hZpoW6c?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=226600258)
And it made me think that, in a time when the price of food has made it so hard for so many of us to get by, we could take a moment to reflect on the fact that on Thanksgiving Day in 2025, [Americans discarded enough food to fill 40 football fields from their Thanksgiving meals](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f0049b-924d-42eb-a7a8-5843fe1a8b67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I think most of us know that in America we waste a lot of food every year. But that sure is a lot, especially for just one day.

Now, I am not shaming anybody. We all do it. It is hard to even think about what to do with the food that is left over, or to plan how much food to buy. Like yesterday, on that trip to the grocery store to get our Thanksgiving ingredients, we went to the meat aisle and I saw a little ham and said to Lucas that maybe we should just get the little one since the kids won't eat that much of it. He agreed. But then, we looked at the price, and it made a lot more sense to buy the big one. It was cheaper!
At the time, we didn't think about the aftermath. We just went for the cheaper option. In this economy, can you blame us? But then, I started thinking, who is going to eat the leftover ham? We are planning on visiting Grammy for the weekend, so we won't be home. Sure, we could try to take some with us, but we expect to stop for a few hours during the drive, and with the luggage, the double stroller, the diaper bag, the books and toys for the road, and a van full of kids, we don't really have the space for a cooler. Also, Grammy probably already made her own food plans for Thanksgiving, and we would only be adding up to her fridge. It just doesn't seem doable for us this time.
We made the mistake (or at least the financial decision) of buying the bigger ham, and I work in a place where there is a whole team of people advocating less food waste, so I cannot plead ignorance when it comes to how big an issue food waste is. According to the research of one of my colleagues, [each year, about 200 million pounds of turkey meat are thrown out over the Thanksgiving holiday week](https://substack.com/redirect/86226673-703e-4d19-b5ab-067414667055?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And it's not just the food. A massive amount of water and energy is used to get the food to our plates. Enough for **every household in America** to run their faucet for 6 hours, or the entire population of Jacksonville, Florida, to get in their own car (even the kids) and drive separately to San Francisco. Nutritionally, **that 's 25.6 billion grams of protein never eaten**--enough to meet more than 500 million adults' recommended daily protein intake, or double the number of adults in the U.S.
So, what can we do? After the grocery run I just told you about, which I imagine goes somewhat similarly for you and your family, I looked for ideas to help us make it less wasteful. But before I get there, if I haven't convinced you that this is important, let me tell you that according to the [Supplemental Poverty Measure (SPM)](https://substack.com/redirect/d91a0ed5-b3a0-42e3-9ce7-cf26c3764160?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which accounts for regional cost-of-living differences, taxes, and government benefits, the combined total of the U.S. population that experiences homelessness (including those in shelters) or lives below the official poverty line sits between 13.1% and 13.3%. That range equals roughly **44.3 million to 45.0 million people** across the United States.
In Missouri, [roughly 711,000 people--or about 11.6% of the state's 6.27 million residents](https://substack.com/redirect/6163ffdc-2548-4206-9b11-1d3702d60424?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--live below the official poverty line or experience homelessness, according to the latest Census ACS data.
Here are some things I am trying to adopt so that I can be better, and I just want to share them with you in case you'd like to, too.
1\. If you haven't done your grocery shopping, **be realistic about your portions**. Avoiding food waste starts long before your meal is on the table. Here's a link to what we call a "[Guest-imator](https://substack.com/redirect/3508a6b7-6a13-458d-901e-2694dbb7393d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," a free online portion calculator that helps you figure out the right amount of food you need to prepare for the size of the party you're hosting, from side dishes to mains, desserts, and even leftovers. And look at what you already have in your kitchen. You might be surprised to find that every year you just get more cans of cranberry sauce when you still have some from last year.
2\. If you already shopped, or better said, overdid it like we did, **make space in your fridge for your Tupperware with leftovers** **and get creative with them**! Coming from a Mexican background, I am planning on trying some ham recipes I've seen online, like a [salsa macha ham](https://substack.com/redirect/4a8480c6-3bb4-4ac1-bc3f-40de009085ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) dish that went viral this week. Or if you have turkey, here's a [turkey pozole](https://substack.com/redirect/331c58de-27b2-4965-b962-2f4a800e915b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recipe I found. If you know dishes made with chicken, you can likely swap in turkey. Could I tempt you to try some turkey [chilaquiles](https://substack.com/redirect/39186868-a920-403e-b017-11db7e06845f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)? (Yummy!) I'm sure if you look, your algorithm will quickly fill your social media with turkey or ham leftover recipes. **If you have guests** , ask them to bring Tupperware so they can take leftovers home.
3\. **Freeze before you toss**. As the shelf life of your leftovers and surplus ingredients comes close to an end, consider popping them in the freezer before it's too late. Nearly [anything can be frozen](https://substack.com/redirect/a6e048c6-151e-4cde-ba4f-93ca4eb9484d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and rediscovered for a dark winter weeknight when you don't have the energy to cook.
4\. **Don 't peel your veggies**! Something I've been adopting in my own cooking is not peeling my potatoes and veggies. Most dishes are just as good with the peel on, and we won't be losing those nutrients. Just make sure to wash them well.
5\. **Finally, share with the less fortunate around you**. My friends and I hosted a Friendsgiving a few years back, and we all brought dishes, which led, of course, to loads of leftovers. We decided to prepare plates and venture out into the cold evening to give them away to the homeless people we saw nearby. Most of them were thrilled to have a warm Thanksgiving meal. Of course, find your own way to do this that feels safe for your family and yourself. Maybe look into local shelters or hospitals near you that are accepting leftover donations. In my Facebook groups, I see a lot of moms in the KC area who are struggling to put a meal on the table for their children and asking for leftovers. In fact, every time I post food on Facebook, I am immediately hit with requests to come pick it up. Truly, if you look, you will find ways to share. Maybe ask in your neighborhood group if anyone has any ideas as to where to donate the food.
As we head into the holiday, Lucas and I hope your family is well. We hope you are all healthy, thriving, and happy. We are thankful for your support of our family, and we will continue to show up as we can for all of you.
Happy Thanksgiving!
Marilyn

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: What I’m thankful for
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
#

Friends --
This year, Thanksgiving follows a few big weeks packed with significant events: Election Day and the rush of Democrats winning up and down the ballot and all across the country, the promise of majorities in the House and Senate that give us the opportunity to demonstrate to the American people what we will do with this new power, and still daily reminders that President Trump remains President of the United States.
That means I have a LOT to reflect on and a long list of things to be grateful for this Thanksgiving.
In the spirit of the holiday, I thought I'd share just a few of them below. This year I am thankful for:
* The almost 5 million Michiganders who turned out to vote for statewide candidates and a Democratic trifecta with the State House and State Senate, and four new members of Congress that helped us flip the House.
* The more than 75,000 of you who donated or signed up to volunteer in our efforts to elect Democrats in tough races in Michigan and across the country. I was asked to help campaign in a number of places Democrats had tough races and you helped fund that work.
* A group of everyday Americans who sat on a grand jury, listened to the Trump Administration's attempt to indict me for making a video the president didn't like and said "no" this is not a crime.
This year was not without loss. At the start of the year we lost my father, Curt Slotkin, to a two-year battle with cancer. He fought hard, but was ready to go. I am thankful that we were with him at home when he passed away – and I am thankful for the friends, families and strangers who helped me through that difficult time.
I’ll be taking a few days with family this week to fully relax, recharge, and be grateful – and I hope you’re able to do the same.
Elissa

PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
P.O. Box 4145
East Lansing, MI 48826
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can [ unsubscribe here](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1&akid=2539%2E135344%2E6KWnGi).

name: Peter Welch
subject: What I’m thankful for this year
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT
body:
On this special day, I hope you’re surrounded by good food and good people, and that you’re able to reflect on what you’re thankful for.

# [](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/144?t=2&akid=1410%2E61531%2EOkAnvk)
Happy Thanksgiving, friends,
It has been a long year, full of ups and downs. Our country and our state have experienced victories and suffered defeats. Through it all, I have so much to be thankful for.
For those who demonstrated against corruption and tyranny.
For those who volunteered their time.
For those who donated to worthy causes.
For those who voted.
For those who advocated for policies and legislation they believe in.
For those who had conversations with their friends and neighbors about what matters to them.
For those who attended one of my listening sessions in Vermont and shared their ideas and concerns.
For those who wrote or called my office.
For the beauty of Vermont.
For the privilege of serving Vermonters in the Senate.
For my family.
For all of you.
I’m thankful for all of it.
On this special day, I hope you’re surrounded by good food and good people, and that you’re able to reflect on what you’re thankful for.
Happy Thanksgiving,
Peter

name: The Democrats
subject: What we’re thankful for this year
body:
Spoiler alert: It’s you [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10378%2E22930333%2Em4BfQo)
---
As our team heads home for Thanksgiving, we’re reflecting on the past year — what Democrats have accomplished, the people who made it possible, and what we’re thankful for. This time last year, the pundits and analysts would’ve said that a 56-seat majority in the Senate would be almost impossible for Democrats to achieve. They had _no idea_ what you would help us accomplish. We’re so grateful for the incredible Democratic candidates who looked around at that environment and decided to _do something about it_. To step up and offer to serve their communities in Congress. To sacrifice time with their families and loved ones to come to Washington and make a difference for their neighbors. For the campaign staff and volunteers who went out and knocked on doors day after day, rain or shine. Who spent hours on their feet, making sure that their neighbors knew what was at stake in this election, and had a plan to get out and vote about it. For our legal team, who worked tirelessly to protect voting rights across the country. Who have stood up to Donald Trump and his administration in court time and time again and are continuing to file briefs and lawsuits to ensure that every eligible American is able to vote in 2027, 2028, and beyond. **And for you, our incredible team of grassroots supporters.** _None_ of the victories Democrats won this month would have been possible without your support. Victories like this one, a once-in-a-generation rebuke of hatred, chaos, and division, couldn’t happen without _millions_ of Americans stepping up to do their part. Thank you for being one of those millions. We’re excited to take on 2028 with this team. To drag Donald Trump, Stephen Miller, and every single member of their corrupt administration kicking and screaming from the White House. We know that with your continued support, we can make it happen. **[DONATE](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&amount=7&refcode=em_20261126_10378_fr&t=5&akid=10378%2E22930333%2Em4BfQo)** Thank you, thank you, thank you. The Democrats

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

name: Governor-elect Aaron Ford
subject: Happy Thanksgiving!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1287%2E127862%2Emm9rIN)
Friends,
I met my wife the day after Thanksgiving in 1994. That’s why Thanksgiving is my favorite time of the year!
Not only do I get to spend time with my motivation — my sons, I also get to reminisce on the first time I met my wife and sit around the table with her and our young men to give thanks for all we have.
I appreciate these moments of togetherness more than ever. To me, Thanksgiving is not about the sales and bargains at the mall, but about the rare moments when my family can come together to break bread and share all for which we are thankful.
This year, I will also be giving thanks for the opportunity to represent Nevada families as their Governor. And it’s an honor and a blessing to serve.
I hope you all enjoy this Thanksgiving holiday with your friends, neighbors and families. Happy Thanksgiving!
Aaron

Josh Shapiro

Socialism Sucks
---
|
---
Spotted this bumper sticker, and it says a lot. 🇺🇸 Socialism often sounds appealing in theory. In practice, when governments take control of production and eliminate private ownership of the means of production, the results have been consistent:
❌ Destroys incentives: When people cannot keep the rewards of their effort and risk-taking, productivity and innovation decline.
❌ Central planning fails: No group of planners can match the information and coordination that free prices and private decisions provide. The result is chronic shortages and waste.
❌ Shrinks liberty: Concentrating economic power in the state almost always expands political control and reduces individual freedom.
❌ Abolishes private property rights: It removes the fundamental right to own, use, and benefit from what you produce.
❌ Produces stagnation and scarcity: Instead of broad prosperity, it has repeatedly delivered shortages, declining living standards, and higher poverty relative to market systems.
❌ Has a grim track record: 20th-century socialist/ communist regimes that implemented these ideas caused tens of millions of deaths through famine, execution, forced labor, and repression (estimates commonly range from the mid-tens of millions to around 100 million). Authoritarianism was the rule, not the exception.
A free-market economy built on secure private property rights and individual liberty, like the United States, has lifted far more people out of poverty than any other system in history. Let's protect the system of freedom that actually works.

How the Federal Withholding of funds Actually Works
Rather than immediately clawing back money already in ACPS's bank account, a federal directive to VDOE typically operates as a reimbursement freeze and high-risk designation:

* School districts usually spend money first and submit invoices to VDOE to be reimbursed from federal grant pools. Under a hold, VDOE pauses those reimbursements to ACPS until the federal conditions are met.

* VDOE has 30 days to submit a statewide corrective action plan showing how it will audit Virginia school districts to ensure hiring and safety laws are followed.

clean_body: | | | == == Happy Thanksgiving! | Team, I am thankful for your trust in me for another term in Congress, and I am thankful for President Donald J. Trump and his team, Governor Glenn Youngkin, 5th District Chair Ramona Christian, and all of our incredible volunteers for helping us pull off a hard-fought victory against a radical and heavily funded, Soros-backed opponent. We are especially thankful for the brave men and women of our military. Thank you for keeping us safe. Fox News The Big Weekend Show | == I joined Tomi Lahren, Johnny Joey Jones, Anita Vogel, and Kevin Corke on Fox News's The Big Weekend Show to break down how the grace of God and the strength of rural Virginia helped us defeat a Soros-backed opponent and overcome the blue wave. We also discussed what needs to happen next regarding Russia and Ukraine, Iran, the Democrats' lawfare plans, and getting real work done in Congress before January 3. == It's Miller Time | == Historically, the party in power faces headwinds in the midterms. The conflict in Iran, combined with Democrats shutting down U.S. refineries for a reckless electric vehicle mandate, left Americans vulnerable to high gas prices. Come January 2027, voters are going to have a massive case of buyer's remorse. We will keep working hard to earn the trust of the middle class and bounce back even stronger in 2028. In the meantime, here is a summary of White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller's remarks on President Trump's accomplishments: ✅ Unprecedented Two-Year Record: Miller states that President Trump has accomplished more in the past two years than any other president in American history, noting that listing every achievement would take hours. ✅ Net Deregulation: He describes Trump as the first president to achieve net deregulation, removing ten regulations for every new one introduced, a milestone he notes was not reached even during the Reagan administration. ✅ Social & Border Policies: Miller highlights the elimination of DEI initiatives and transgender policies, the securing of the border, record deportations, and historically low crime and low murder rates. ✅ Energy & Trade: He points to record domestic production of fossil fuels and coal, the activation of the first new nuclear reactors since the 1970s, and the rebalancing of global trade relationships. ✅ National Security & Foreign Policy: Miller cites the rebuilding of the U.S. military and federal law enforcement, the use of lethal force against drug cartels, a rapid takeover of Venezuela that doubled U.S. oil reserves, and reshaped diplomatic relationships with both Russia and China. ✅ Economic Performance: He credits the administration with building the strongest economy and fastest wage growth in U.S. history while overcoming the high inflation and perceived international standing issues inherited from the Biden administration. ✅ Looking Ahead: Concluding his remarks, Miller predicts that the upcoming two years will be the greatest in American history and expresses pride in serving as White House Chief of Staff to continue delivering results. == Weekly Recap - Protecting Virginia's Children | == here is a troubling pattern of child endangerment in the Albemarle County school system, and we are seeing similar failures in Alexandria and across the Commonwealth. Watch my recent interview with 29 News in Charlottesville to hear what we are doing to hold leadership accountable: == Socialism Sucks | Spotted this bumper sticker, and it says a lot. 🇺🇸 Socialism often sounds appealing in theory. In practice, when governments take control of production and eliminate private ownership of the means of production, the results have been consistent: ❌ Destroys incentives: When people cannot keep the rewards of their effort and risk-taking, productivity and innovation decline. ❌ Central planning fails: No group of planners can match the information and coordination that free prices and private decisions provide. The result is chronic shortages and waste. ❌ Shrinks liberty: Concentrating economic power in the state almost always expands political control and reduces individual freedom. ❌ Abolishes private property rights: It removes the fundamental right to own, use, and benefit from what you produce. ❌ Produces stagnation and scarcity: Instead of broad prosperity, it has repeatedly delivered shortages, declining living standards, and higher poverty relative to market systems. ❌ Has a grim track record: 20th-century socialist/ communist regimes that implemented these ideas caused tens of millions of deaths through famine, execution, forced labor, and repression (estimates commonly range from the mid-tens of millions to around 100 million). Authoritarianism was the rule, not the exception. A free-market economy built on secure private property rights and individual liberty, like the United States, has lifted far more people out of poverty than any other system in history. Let's protect the system of freedom that actually works. Newsmax Interview | == Under Speaker Mike Johnson's leadership, House Republicans passed over 1,000 bills, and roughly 700 of those measures are still awaiting Senate action. Republicans focus on how we're going to make life better for hardworking Americans, while Democrats focus on who they're going to target next. Come January, expect Washington to be bogged down in endless partisan investigations. == The Schilling Show: John McGuire | == We will never stop fighting to protect children. Today I had the honor of joining the Rob Schilling Show in Charlottesville to talk about the ongoing failures to protect children in Albemarle County Schools. == Albemarle County School Funding? | == How the Federal Withholding of funds Actually Works Rather than immediately clawing back money already in ACPS's bank account, a federal directive to VDOE typically operates as a reimbursement freeze and high-risk designation: School districts usually spend money first and submit invoices to VDOE to be reimbursed from federal grant pools. Under a hold, VDOE pauses those reimbursements to ACPS until the federal conditions are met. VDOE has 30 days to submit a statewide corrective action plan showing how it will audit Virginia school districts to ensure hiring and safety laws are followed. == Why Did Spanberger Opt Out of School Tax Credits? | == Why did Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger opt out of the new Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program for 2027, reversing former Governor Glenn Youngkin's initial move to enroll the state? name: Squad Victory Fund
subject: Wishing you a happy Thanksgiving, Peter
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20261126-2986-foote&t=1001&akid=2986%2E342411%2ECbXxKv ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter, happy
Thanksgiving! Before the day gets busy, we want to say something: thank
you.

This cycle, Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida all won their races.
Every one of those wins came from this team: you stayed in this fight when
it would have been easier to tune out. We couldn’t be more grateful to
have you by our side.

And the Squad didn't wait long to get back to work. Over the past few
weeks, they and their teams have been out at turkey drives, clothing
drives, and food pantries in their districts, packing boxes and handing
out meals so more families can sit down together this holiday season.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/20576?t=1002&akid=2986%2E342411%2ECbXxKv ]Images of the Squad and their teams at turkey and clothing drives and
food pantries.

The Squad knows what so many of our neighbors are up against. SNAP and
other assistance programs are being rolled back. Groceries cost more than
they did a year ago. Rent, utilities, and everyday bills keep taking a
bigger share of every paycheck. More families are figuring out how to
stretch a holiday meal, or whether they can put one together at all.

And it isn't only happening here. In countries across the globe, families
are facing hunger driven by conflict, disaster, and rising costs. So
today, we're not asking you to give to us.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/20576?t=1003&akid=2986%2E342411%2ECbXxKv ]If you're able, will you make a donation to World Central Kitchen to
help get meals to families who need them most?

DONATE TO WORLD CENTRAL KITCHEN ››

World Central Kitchen gets fresh meals to communities in crisis around the
world. You can give to their work anywhere: a country where you have
family, a place you've been following in the news, or a community you
can't stop thinking about. Wherever you choose, it's one more family that
gets to share a meal this season.

This time of year is about pulling up another chair and making sure nobody
goes without. That's how this movement works too. None of us gets through
alone, and all of us are stronger when we take care of each other.

From all of us here, we hope you have a safe and joyful holiday, and we're
so glad you're with us.

With gratitude and solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

Contributions or gifts to The Squad Victory Fund are not tax deductible.

Contributions to The Squad Victory Fund will be allocated equally among: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, Rashida Tlaib for Congress, Courage to Change, Inspiring Leadership Has a Name PAC, Power of Us PAC, and Rooted in Community Leadership PAC.

Any contributor may designate their contribution for a particular participant. The allocation formula above may change if any contributor makes a contribution that, when allocated, would exceed the amount that the contributor may lawfully give to any participant.

After contributing to The Squad Victory Fund, you will automatically be signed up to receive email updates from Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, and Rashida Tlaib for Congress. You may of course opt-out by unsubscribing at any time.

This Thanksgiving, I'm so beyond thankful for this movement.
This is Rep. Patricia "Pat" Moore (D-LA), and I want to tell you something I don't say often enough.
I grew up in public housing. When I was a girl, nobody looked at me and saw a future member of Congress. Honestly, I didn't either – I’m only in this place because of the help of my family, my community, and my faith.
And yet here I am, 16 days away from becoming the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress.
I never expected to be standing on this doorstep. And I know exactly who carried me here: you.
More than 156,000 contributions to this historic campaign. All fueled by teachers. Nurses. Retirees. Doctors. Janitors. Folks from every corner of this country, giving what they can, when they can.
**_Our average donation? Just $17._**
[](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001g5fWZ1Wtw2tjR-JK0Mdbp_isLnGgBc526-dBF1aMacvYhvXhRVZfp57wGpKAF8HgdxS_6QPHFB_2jtbosh5T3GruUkaV9K6RJQivoYx_dGemYz5IT8y3_6f3NhyXbibLTdQf-FprCHS64DxE_oy0Rjo2C_8bb6PtMG6BsqpjtfEjkzvadJAIeT8oAG0BxMBj1dwqSqCOBrnW-Ho1j8fFDParl5rjf4wFYJyk-T8szbkVWNRD2JKXBw==&c=5CSdQo9DZ8pwsbHnv7f_iwdUmIIQoiW4AoiQPpvfGQ3Qvtj7IIXlMA==&ch=Xq0WzKOlWxxpDa4qoJTGUM6qcBQa20CdNl5tM-S2HkoykjQnn_w8Uw==)
---
This campaign doesn't belong to anybody powerful. It belongs to the people.
And that's _exactly_ what scares the other side.
Right now, Super PACs, corporate special interests, and data center companies are lining up to buy this race. They think a seat in Congress is just another thing that's for sale.
**We're going to prove them wrong. Dead wrong.**
**So this Thanksgiving week, I'm asking: Will you chip in $17, our average donation, to show this seat isn't for sale? And if $17 is too much right now, even $1 sends the same message. Every single gift is a vote of confidence that this runoff will be decided by folks like you, not by the highest bidder.**

body:
Share this message with your loved ones...

| | | |
---
| | | Fellow Conservative, As we gather around the table this Thanksgiving, I am reminded yet again of the providential voyage that the Pilgrims made more than four hundred years ago... In September of 1620, the Pilgrims set sail on the _Mayflower_ , leaving behind everything familiar so they could live in freedom and worship freely as devoted Christians. **Their dream of freedom was really the first American Dream.** As **President Calvin Coolidge** once said on the three-hundredth anniversary of the Pilgrims' landing at Plymouth: _" Plymouth Rock does not mark a beginning or an end. It marks a revelation of that which is without beginning and without end: a purpose, shining through eternity with a resplendent light..." __ _ **That resplendent light was quick to take hold in America.** The Pilgrims signed the _Mayflower Compact_ before they even set foot on shore. In it they agreed to form a "civil body politic" and to make and obey just laws for themselves. That simple yet visionary agreement helped give birth to the spirit of American self-governance that we still enjoy. **In America today, we enjoy blessings that the Pilgrims were yearning for:** the freedom to worship Almighty God, to speak our minds freely, and to live under the protection of our rights as self-governing Americans. Those freedoms were won and kept by the sacrifice of many generations, and they should never be taken for granted. **Remembering our history and safeguarding America for the next generation: that 's my purpose and my promise to you, today and all days. ** _With best wishes for you and your whole family: Happy Thanksgiving!_ Ted Cruz

This Thanksgiving, I wanted to take a quick moment to say thank you.
Throughout this year’s campaign, I’ve been incredibly touched by seeing the immense potential for genuine connection and collaboration, even in these divided times.
I've been reflecting on how we all share a common hope: that together, we can meet the challenges our communities face. That's why I'm especially grateful for neighbors like you who believe in the power of bringing people together to make government work better for everyone.
Your support – whether through a kind message, a conversation at a community event, or a contribution to our campaign – reminds me that when we focus on our shared values rather than our differences, we can accomplish extraordinary things.
As I celebrate this Thanksgiving with my family, I'm filled with gratitude for this opportunity to serve and for supporters like you who make this work possible.
Wishing you and your loved ones a wonderful Thanksgiving,
Sarah McBride

## Your Thanksgiving Memories
This Thanksgiving Day, we are so grateful for all of you who shared Thanksgiving memories with us. Two stood out. Trey from Boca Raton took us back 54 years to one of the last full family dinners at his grandparents' house. After the meal, the den erupted into a family argument. He remembers his grandfather, 6-foot-3, had slipped out without a word when the fighting started, but then reappeared in the doorway after it had finally calmed down to say, "Well, I think..." and set the room off again. He caught Trey's eye, winked, and walked back out. Penny from Ocala flew to Washington, D.C., for Thanksgiving 2024 to see her youngest, an Army intelligence officer deploying to Germany that January. The next day they cut down a Christmas tree at a Maryland farm in the freezing cold and enjoyed hot cider. They still talk about how hard they laughed together, especially when she fell into the tree and could not get up. Her son is still overseas, and she can't wait to see him again. We wish you all good memories this Thanksgiving and good times with family near and far, whether this year or down the road.

Florida State can clinch bowl eligibility Friday at Doak Campbell Stadium with its first win over No. 20 Florida since 2023. ABC will broadcast the rivals’ [70th meeting](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkMFuhCAYhJ8GbxhAQT1w6MXb9tqj-Su_ShfBwF_Nvn2zm_YJeptkMpNv5uM23cAHH9d32NEuaZkiXiUgEeaJNoj3svrTx5W29L1uVJaQsp-UUIZLyZWZYCZ_4tRC5WzX9iA-K7SyG7QZhNZDtVln5NAsZui1Ma4F1ErMToBz_dJJM8-Vt88-KZWRQms91MvcAyoEYwRg3xjWCnSeUq6_ko9LeKQT84vEQT2nvQp2IzoKa96YGpkar-uqU2yeHlPjkRNT43MYU-NvjAPxP1kICPmRwmOHfEfiybnC04HRx5UfyUfi5cgIjmc8EQI6vqWLU-IX0LwxNVbZuuPyIfhiOtaKdQcfXmj0z1dPq34CAAD__6wNkDc). body:
Dear Peter, I wanted to send a note to wish you and your loved ones a _very Happy Thanksgiving. _ Thanksgiving is my absolute favorite holiday because I love coming together around a shared meal with family and friends, appreciating the small things, and all we have to be thankful for. This year, I’m particularly thankful for my family, especially my husband, Mike, and our son, Jack. I’m thankful for every Vermonter who put their trust in me and voted to send me back to the Lieutenant Governor’s office. I’m thankful for the opportunity to work for our state, communities and Vermonters again, and for every supporter, volunteer, advisor, staffer and friend I met across Vermont this year who helped make this possible. My hope for today, and for the year ahead, is that we can find our way back to the simple things: **appreciating what each of us has to offer and making sure the basic needs of every member of our community are met.** To that end, Vermont Public put together a terrific list of places across Vermont offering free Thanksgiving meals today. ## Readers Share Thanksgiving Memories
Thanks to everyone who shared favorite Thanksgiving memories with us. Here are three we loved. Sandi recalls the annual spread of pies—apple, pumpkin, lemon meringue, and chocolate cream—and her uncle who loved them all. _“Mom would ask Uncle Charlie what kind of pie he wanted. Uncle Charlie always said the same thing: ‘I’ll take a piece of each.’”_ Suzanne remembers celebrations that lasted throughout Thanksgiving week. _“My dad’s birthday is November 26, so we always included a celebration of his birthday as part of our Thanksgiving dinner. Then on November 30, we marked the occasion of my parents’ wedding anniversary. They were married 67 years.”_ Elizabeth from Apex remembers the year her dad hoped to visit for the holiday but called to say he wasn’t able to make it. When the call suddenly went silent, two hands grabbed her shoulders from behind. _“It was my dad! He had tricked me into thinking he couldn’t come, but arrived just in time for dinner!”_

## Snowflakes Could Fall This Thanksgiving

clean_body: A storm system that brought a much-needed soaking of 1 to 2 inches of rain to Middle Tennessee lingers through Thanksgiving, with colder air allowing rain to mix with snow today. | | | | | | Thursday, November 26, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning, and happy Thanksgiving! On this day in 1939, was born Anna Mae Bullock in Brownsville and grew up in nearby Nutbush. She later immortalized her hometown in the 1973 hit Nutbush City Limits on her way to becoming the "Queen of Rock 'n' Roll." However you're spending Thanksgiving, we hope it brings peace, gratitude, and second helpings. Today's edition of The Tennessee Flyover is running a bit shorter as our team takes time to celebrate with loved ones. Also, please keep an eye out for tomorrow's special Flyover Christmas Gift Guide , filled with dozens of great gift ideas for every member of your family. What's the fastest way to ruin Thanksgiving dinner? It's usually not the turkey. One wrong question at the table can do more damage than any overcooked bird. Today, we're counting down five things you shouldn't bring up at Thanksgiving and five conversation starters that actually work. So which topic seems harmless but never ends well? And what gets even the quietest person at the table talking? Check out The Flyover Podcast to see the full list before you sit down to dinner. ! **Happy Thanksgiving!** On this day in 1789, the nation celebrated its [first Thanksgiving](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGnMR3IHsDgwsVt6Pa2KdEsHmAUg1dmZLRvH21eIcVpP-n8X4_5gRz53P7jQV7KOp90X5FEKM9LwkswXpLygTlzoUt2PL-vGTTY2pga7IyLcKG5wyr4FTtCV5E3g-utM30P1e4DrvrpHMI4Wgpj24-4Uj-0bavBge4q9h_PmM8MtLoZOrS2GzEE40zrtOo0BZaUG9mpcN74ZFzjOxXKzZKOKvpd5HWp9p-CScF033cT09JsqSiYWOhQMEkK-K75rHf-XHormM5U6HhSrsEqmKrsw-vmGPmyg-r0diDHX1_-mKZ4-AkAAP__1qJ4sA) under the Constitution, a day of 'publick thanksgiving and prayer' proclaimed by Virginia-born President George Washington. ## Storm Complicates Virginia Thanksgiving Travel
A coastal storm is [bringing heavy rain](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnTAQRb8GunnCBgwuXKTZbtOmRAOeB6MYs7InRvx9xIue8gFbjHSlka7Oub8-p0_kwHH9iTs5Kc8p0pkDiVCalgOzYMhypB1T4kJZNoy_86QbbUAp0GbCRbjQ1GHt3RM7QluTU4PtjVV9r-vNGRr0aNAu7WiGcegGa-a-H3s9k0Jr55rd3afUfUq3zWPo0JhuRO-VVa1tqq4hz3Kkh2xUOK0cGZ_hOgqlx3LsdXCbyFeu2h-V_qj0x5lJ7scdCWWj9D8BBkoCHi94mcGcOK4ZNsJyQUKOgNHD-ifLBSdHn-GI8E985cJxhTcCvCvjUWifKcEtUifnv04OgbMZqq5Zd-TwwpRvLlyc_hsAAP___JyUWw), strong winds, and tidal flooding to Virginia on Thanksgiving, complicating holiday travel across the Commonwealth. Rain moved in Wednesday and is expected to be [heaviest Thursday morning](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkTHOpDoQhE8DmUe4xxg7IHgJ2f_SDVGP3R5aa-yRacH-t1-xyR5gg5JKqlJJn-rH1_qFnLm8_8edZjnTWug6MolQW0PFQzAfUtuOrfFJh2xYfh4rDGCV1grsikH4pNVgH-eEhtD3NOvJj9brcYR-m0cTjEspOQ8jRucsgJ0svHwcQrLTq-f53tP6lobn8JgMWmscxqi9fvqhMwNFltoestHJ7c2FMeXvelJ7hLr3ed5EPkf3_K-DpYPluq6Hft4opV53o4MFm3DIdKeEslH76xTvHwzSwdKQi7q4xENhiUo4YlYp1xq5vBX9-lAQikqqwpQoiNpq5ojfShqelDtYwGuFKaYQ7aRGek3KRDcq9wKnko2DSc4PBFPf5vi5OGc-7NSZ4b0j5z8w8o8_nDP8DgAA__9WGJ3m), with 1 to 3 inches forecast inland and 3 to 5 inches near the coast. The strongest winds and highest water levels are expected around the Thursday morning high tide. Gusts of [30 to 60 mph](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAMhp8GNhAxuXAZMnRhu64dkS8YsC7AKbGI7u0rrlVfoIOH359k-f--bsMNOfA2f-JKTo5p2CinQCIUB79jEgxJ9rhijHxQkgW3RxqgAVMpVYEZ0AsfNGgsRzehJrQlOdXZi7HqcoFycXfVoCFrO7Ae2uukvbmPHbSgG2yvnkp25z2lzlHQNnWn0Rh9xXFUVrW2KXRDI8sea1no4DjzxjiF135QrP2-lsEtIs9UtB8F9AX0Oec6y-MNz0goC8UCetlHfKVq2iN5TFJAP3FMUmWMG2_zH6gkon-cG6x-Os98nPHXSfWWUkY3PjOHwMl0hW7mFTm8H5J_ujwcfAcAAP__OSGNRg) are possible along the coast. Moderate to major coastal flooding is forecast for vulnerable parts of Hampton Roads and tidal river areas, and some roads could close. Power outages are also possible. Dominion Energy staged crews ahead of the storm and plans to [limit bucket-truck work](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhSAQRb8GOwwg6FpQbGP3tt3SzBPUySIYmGDe32982T_YYorJSW7uPd-P-QEYMG5fcHhLdZ2jv0rwRD7PS4JCEAqlfEDOWH2hHeJPmZVQPZeSq36GhbD6WUPj7Araw9h4K4fR9KM0RjW7fYJ2YgAxGGN6L1bpBqck6KfSxkDXNWjvPCnvk6oT7aCh7_UHOCdH2Y2CaeEdUsot7b5i3jAirOGVqs_tko4m2J3oLKz7ZGpiarquq72gvm7I1HRvYmoKaYHA_x7Cs_A1p4O7dGDEFHmK_Mz-hIxx42vKnHbPMS433_hbA1NTk607LwwBSz8wLbYDMLxb0D8FVqt-AwAA__-NK4fX) while winds exceed 35 mph. Travelers are urged to allow extra time and avoid flooded roadways. Conditions are expected to improve Thursday afternoon and evening as the system moves out.
## Virginians Recall Past Thanksgivings
Thanks to everyone who shared their favorite Thanksgiving memories with us. Here are two we loved. Robert wrote: "While in the Air Force, we used to have some of the troops over for a home-cooked dinner when we were in Okinawa, North Carolina, and when we were in Northern Virginia while stationed at the Pentagon. The younger, single troops really enjoyed getting to go 'home' for a family dinner on Thanksgiving. Military members take care of their own. It's a close family." Ludford recalls a Thanksgiving when his grandmother came and offered to help with the cooking and baking. "As the meal came together, there was a new aroma in the kitchen ... unusual but a really nice smell. When we sat down to eat, the new food was placed on the table. The new dish caught Daddy by surprise. He watched as it was scooped up and asked, 'What is that stuff?' My grandmother said, 'That is Maine turkey--we call it lasagna'." Whether you're dining on turkey or lasagna today, we hope you get a second helping!

## Menu That Hasn't Changed Since 1997
I haven't been allowed to change our Thanksgiving menu since 1997! After ten years of marriage, I made our entire Thanksgiving dinner using recipes from the November 1997 issue of _Bon App etit_, which was my favorite cooking magazine at the time. The meal includes a brown sugar and spice-cured turkey, sausage cornbread stuffing with cilantro, and a tart cherry apple pie, along with other traditional side dishes and desserts. The stuffing became such a family favorite that I now have to make three trays just to ensure we have enough leftovers, including for fried eggs over stuffing the next morning. After almost 30 years, it still brings me so much joy to see my family, and now our extended family, enjoy this meal every year. We've built a strong tradition that I hope gets passed down to future generations. In fact, just two days ago, my husband asked if we could make the stuffing on a random weekday! _Caroline, Garden City, New York_
## Clark's Pecan Pie
My brother-in-law died of cancer 25 years ago, but we still talk about him every November. Clark lived alone after a divorce and never learned to cook anything. His favorite dessert was pecan pie, but there was no one left in his life to make one. Then one day, he found the perfect pecan pie recipe in a magazine at a doctor's office. He bought the ingredients and learned to make that one dish. Year after year, we were treated to several pecan pies, enough for each family to take one home. He also gave us the leftover pecans because he had no use for them until the next Thanksgiving. We have all learned to make Clark's pecan pie, and we love the memory of him arriving with the only homemade dish he ever cooked. _Teresa, Coldspring, Texas_
## Thanksgiving Crash Landing
My husband and I had been married for a few years when we finally got up the nerve to host our extended family for Thanksgiving dinner. Everything was ready. All the food was on the table: turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes, sweet potatoes, and vegetables. Everyone was seated and passing dishes around when, all of a sudden, BOOM! The ceiling fan over the dining room table fell right out of the ceiling and landed in the middle of all the food! The baby started crying in her high chair, everyone gasped, and then everything went completely quiet. Finally, after the dust settled, my aunt said, "Well, let's clear this mess and finish dinner!" So we all jumped up, the guys moved the ceiling fan off the table, the girls cleaned up the rest of the mess, and we finished our Thanksgiving dinner! True story! _Linda, Merritt Island, Florida_
## Pie for My Brother
When my brother was alive, he loved cooking recipes from the 1800s in cast iron over a campfire. He died suddenly at age 53, but one of his recipes has remained a Thanksgiving tradition. It is a double-crust cranberry pie, a very simple recipe made with chopped fresh cranberries, raisins, a little sugar, and flour for thickening. Since my brother's passing, I have taken on the role of making it every year. My husband doesn't like cranberries, but he loves this pie. And every Thanksgiving, I vent the top crust with my brother's initials. _Terry, Frisco, Texas_
## Thanksgiving at Grandma's
When we were children living on Long Island, we would go to our grandmother's house the night before Thanksgiving and sleep on cots next to a steam radiator. It was nice and warm, and the radiator made the most soothing noises. There were always Hershey bars in the cabinet and an old-fashioned clock that ticked away. In the morning, my sister and I would wake up early to help Grandma and Mom prepare the Thanksgiving feast. In the background, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade played on the console television. Since we are Italian, our feast included both Italian and American foods. Naturally, turkey was at the center of the meal, but we started with pasta and a relish dish of fennel, olives, artichoke hearts, and celery. Our stuffing was made with Italian bread, Parmesan, provolone, and eggs. There were mushrooms sauteed in garlic and olive oil, cranberry sauce, pies, fresh fruit, chocolates, and cordials. Our meals lasted for hours! Between dinner and dessert, my brothers, sister, and I would argue over whether to watch football or Laurel and Hardy's _March of the Wooden Soldiers_. Those were the days. Our Thanksgivings were so memorable that I eventually bought a DVD of _March of the Wooden Soldiers_ just to bring a little of my childhood back to Thanksgiving. _LuAnn, Wake Forest, North Carolina_

On this day in 1789, Americans marked the under the new Constitution, a Thursday President George Washington set aside at the request of Congress. He spent it at church in New York City and sent beer and food to the city's jailed debtors. Happy Thanksgiving! Today's holiday edition is a little different. Instead of our usual lineup of news stories, we're sharing five Thanksgiving memories from our readers, filled with family traditions, laughter, and heartfelt moments. You'll still find the latest news in Quick Hits below and you can read more Thanksgiving memories . What's the fastest way to ruin Thanksgiving dinner? It's usually not the turkey. One wrong question at the table can do more damage than any overcooked bird. Today, we're counting down five things you shouldn't bring up at Thanksgiving and five conversation starters that actually work. So which topic seems harmless but never ends well? And what gets even the quietest person at the table talking? Check out The Flyover Podcast to see the full list before you sit down to dinner. ! Also, please keep an eye out for tomorrow's special Flyover Christmas Gift Guide , filled with dozens of great gift ideas for every member of your family. Today's sponsor, , has a Black Friday gift for the health-curious on your list: a $169 at-home DNA test that pairs personalized insights with research on peptides and supplements. | Menu That Hasn't Changed Since 1997 I haven't been allowed to change our Thanksgiving menu since 1997! After ten years of marriage, I made our entire Thanksgiving dinner using recipes from the November 1997 issue of Bon App etit, which was my favorite cooking magazine at the time. The meal includes a brown sugar and spice-cured turkey, sausage cornbread stuffing with cilantro, and a tart cherry apple pie, along with other traditional side dishes and desserts. The stuffing became such a family favorite that I now have to make three trays just to ensure we have enough leftovers, including for fried eggs over stuffing the next morning. After almost 30 years, it still brings me so much joy to see my family, and now our extended family, enjoy this meal every year. We've built a strong tradition that I hope gets passed down to future generations. In fact, just two days ago, my husband asked if we could make the stuffing on a random weekday! Caroline, Garden City, New York Clark's Pecan Pie My brother-in-law died of cancer 25 years ago, but we still talk about him every November. Clark lived alone after a divorce and never learned to cook anything. His favorite dessert was pecan pie, but there was no one left in his life to make one. Then one day, he found the perfect pecan pie recipe in a magazine at a doctor's office. He bought the ingredients and learned to make that one dish. Year after year, we were treated to several pecan pies, enough for each family to take one home. He also gave us the leftover pecans because he had no use for them until the next Thanksgiving. We have all learned to make Clark's pecan pie, and we love the memory of him arriving with the only homemade dish he ever cooked. Teresa, Coldspring, Texas Thanksgiving Crash Landing My husband and I had been married for a few years when we finally got up the nerve to host our extended family for Thanksgiving dinner. Everything was ready. All the food was on the table: turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes, sweet potatoes, and vegetables. Everyone was seated and passing dishes around when, all of a sudden, BOOM! The ceiling fan over the dining room table fell right out of the ceiling and landed in the middle of all the food! The baby started crying in her high chair, everyone gasped, and then everything went completely quiet. Finally, after the dust settled, my aunt said, "Well, let's clear this mess and finish dinner!" So we all jumped up, the guys moved the ceiling fan off the table, the girls cleaned up the rest of the mess, and we finished our Thanksgiving dinner! True story! Linda, Merritt Island, Florida Pie for My Brother When my brother was alive, he loved cooking recipes from the 1800s in cast iron over a campfire. He died suddenly at age 53, but one of his recipes has remained a Thanksgiving tradition. It is a double-crust cranberry pie, a very simple recipe made with chopped fresh cranberries, raisins, a little sugar, and flour for thickening. Since my brother's passing, I have taken on the role of making it every year. My husband doesn't like cranberries, but he loves this pie. And every Thanksgiving, I vent the top crust with my brother's initials. Terry, Frisco, Texas Thanksgiving at Grandma's When we were children living on Long Island, we would go to our grandmother's house the night before Thanksgiving and sleep on cots next to a steam radiator. It was nice and warm, and the radiator made the most soothing noises. There were always Hershey bars in the cabinet and an old-fashioned clock that ticked away. In the morning, my sister and I would wake up early to help Grandma and Mom prepare the Thanksgiving feast. In the background, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade played on the console television. Since we are Italian, our feast included both Italian and American foods. Naturally, turkey was at the center of the meal, but we started with pasta and a relish dish of fennel, olives, artichoke hearts, and celery. Our stuffing was made with Italian bread, Parmesan, provolone, and eggs. There were mushrooms sauteed in garlic and olive oil, cranberry sauce, pies, fresh fruit, chocolates, and cordials. Our meals lasted for hours! Between dinner and dessert, my brothers, sister, and I would argue over whether to watch football or Laurel and Hardy's March of the Wooden Soldiers. Those were the days. Our Thanksgivings were so memorable that I eventually bought a DVD of March of the Wooden Soldiers just to bring a little of my childhood back to Thanksgiving. This season is a welcome opportunity to slow down, gather around the table, and reflect on the people and communities that make this country such a special place to call home.
Every day, I am grateful for the resilience, generosity, and neighborly spirit I see in our community and am eternally grateful for the opportunity to represent you every day in Congress.
Whether you are traveling to visit family, hosting friends at home, or working through the holiday to keep our community safe and running, thank you for all that you do.
From my family to yours, I wish you a Thanksgiving filled with love, peace, and happiness.

## Your Thanksgiving Memories
This Thanksgiving Day, we are grateful for all of you, including the readers who shared their Thanksgiving memories with us. Tancy from Plano told of gathering with 30 other Thanksgiving "orphans" far from home to celebrate an early version of Friendsgiving. Others spoke of food wins, such as DeAnna's grandma's green chile-infused grits and apple pie--and food losses, like when John's mom dropped the turkey upside down on the floor on the way to the table, then calmly picked it up and said she would go get the "other turkey" before bringing the same bird right back out. Betty Sue started making potato salad for 60 on Thanksgiving morning and delivered her baby boy by 3:30 p.m. that afternoon, during the Cowboys game. Ed spent Thanksgiving 1968 clearing a landing zone in the Vietnamese jungle so a helicopter could bring in a hot meal. And Lori's father, gone now more than 20 years, recited the same poem before every Thanksgiving meal, learned in grade school in the 1920s and remembered long after he'd forgotten what he ate for breakfast: _Turkey, oh a great big fellow_
_Rich and brown and oh so mellow_
_All the things that are good to eat,_
_More than I can now repeat_
_That's Thanksgiving!_

clean_body: This Thanksgiving Day, we are grateful for all of you, including the readers who shared their Thanksgiving memories with us. | | | | | | Thursday, November 26, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1835, Texan forces defeated a group of Mexican cavalrymen in the . name: Wesley Bell (personal)
subject: This Thanksgiving, I want to thank you
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter, _**Happy Thanksgiving!**_

Before the day gets away from us, I wanted to take a moment to reach out and say something simple: Thank you. This year has given me so much to be grateful for, and at the top of that list are the people who have stood beside me and believed in the work we're doing together.

When I look back on everything we've accomplished, I'm reminded that none of it happened because of one person. Every step forward was made possible by people who showed up, gave their time, believed in our communities, and worked to make things better. _And I want you to know how much that means to me._

Serving the people of St. Louis is one of the greatest honors of my life. And as we look ahead to a new chapter with a blue Congress, I'm more hopeful than ever about what we can accomplish together. But today isn't about politics or the work ahead. It's about slowing down, spending time with the people we love, and appreciating the things that matter most. I hope you get to do exactly that today. From my family to yours, I wish you a peaceful, joyful, and very happy Thanksgiving.

With gratitude,

Wesley

Happy Thanksgiving! I hope that you're having a great holiday with family and friends.
A number of years ago, I learned that making a list of things that you're grateful for and reviewing it every day improves your frame of mind. You can add something every day that's small, like "I'm glad that today's sunny" or "I'm grateful that I get to see my Mom today." Some of them can be big, like "I'm grateful that I'm healthy and can enjoy traveling" or "I'm glad that I have a roof over my head."
I made this list. It has dozens of items on it. It works. Looking at it does make me feel better.
The list is now a file on my phone. I don't review or add to it every day, but every time I look at it I come away feeling more positive.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/66ab2879-f1c4-40b8-8e79-64de507cf183?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There's a lot of rich data around gratitude as an incredibly powerful feeling. You hear it sometimes from people who have an illness or setback: "I'm just glad that I get to see another day." When you remember what you have, it gives you a rosier perspective.
Seriously - take 5 or 10 minutes and make this list. What better day to do this than Thanksgiving?
People ask me how I'm feeling or doing all of the time. I have a TON to be grateful for, but I also have a lot on my plate most all of the time. It can be easy to get harried or stressed. I remind myself that I'm in a rare position where I've chosen the work that I do; I've already had more success than I would have imagined possible when I was young, and now everything I do is trying to make good things happen.
These are also the golden years during which my parents are still healthy and my kids are old enough to remember trips. I'm vital and strong. Not every year will be this good.
I should be trying to enjoy this time. There's so much to be thankful for.
Do you have good things or people going on in your life? Things you're looking forward to, big or small? I bet you do. Appreciate them, or maybe give yourself one. I regularly find small things to get excited about. It's one reason why I still go out to see movies; it's fun to make them into occasions. Next up is probably Dune 3 or Avengers: Doomsday. I'm a simple person.
I'm grateful for everyone who is reading this and has supported me. Thank you. See how it works? :-)
Have a wonderful Thanksgiving. - Andrew

clean_body: Happy Thanksgiving! | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | ---|---|--- * | | | Nov 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | Happy Thanksgiving! I hope that you're having a great holiday with family and friends. A number of years ago, I learned that making a list of things that you're grateful for and reviewing it every day improves your frame of mind. You can add something every day that's small, like "I'm glad that today's sunny" or "I'm grateful that I get to see my Mom today." Some of them can be big, like "I'm grateful that I'm healthy and can enjoy traveling" or "I'm glad that I have a roof over my head." I made this list. It has dozens of items on it. It works. Looking at it does make me feel better. The list is now a file on my phone. I don't review or add to it every day, but every time I look at it I come away feeling more positive. | | ---|---|--- There's a lot of rich data around gratitude as an incredibly powerful feeling. You hear it sometimes from people who have an illness or setback: "I'm just glad that I get to see another day." When you remember what you have, it gives you a rosier perspective. Seriously - take 5 or 10 minutes and make this list. What better day to do this than Thanksgiving? People ask me how I'm feeling or doing all of the time. I have a TON to be grateful for, but I also have a lot on my plate most all of the time. It can be easy to get harried or stressed. I remind myself that I'm in a rare position where I've chosen the work that I do; I've already had more success than I would have imagined possible when I was young, and now everything I do is trying to make good things happen. These are also the golden years during which my parents are still healthy and my kids are old enough to remember trips. I'm vital and strong. Not every year will be this good. I should be trying to enjoy this time. There's so much to be thankful for. Do you have good things or people going on in your life? Things you're looking forward to, big or small? I bet you do. Appreciate them, or maybe give yourself one. I regularly find small things to get excited about. It's one reason why I still go out to see movies; it's fun to make them into occasions. Next up is probably Dune 3 or Avengers: Doomsday. I'm a simple person. I'm grateful for everyone who is reading this and has supported me. Thank you. See how it works? :-) Have a wonderful Thanksgiving. - Andrew | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Andrew Yang 111 Sutter Street, 7th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

## Wildcats Win Maui Title
No. 8 Arizona [rallied to beat Ole Miss 84-73](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO3DAMRb9G7jSwKI8fhYo07jZtSoOWOGNi9BhYXBu7Xx84SL4gHYtL8pz762P5QI6cnz8xkRP8fiyZzhpJhPZlw_f7SzbMr_rkg_MTE36ysCzQQq-N0dAv6IUPWjpsgrO9n4auIWeG6d5Po7VDszljJuNHY-5j6NehHQEtWN-10A040jQ07K57xkBvbHu3cFtxtBTCMPowQh9IdS0FlrLfZCPc-btkfMSvctB-8yU10W0i76rsDwWzgvlv5OQYPEq9Mgrmy0zBfP1SMBtzzXcFc6Jc9Yr1RbJijPrfmvYROelH-dxl05e65nywoHDJGLWwRNIny6Z9SbSif-mTs76wdImkE9fa7C68T46Raz-orn0m5PgHWv6378PB7wAAAP__FVuYAw) Wednesday for its fourth Maui Invitational championship. ## Gravy Problem Solved
When my grandson was about 9, he rode his bike to my house announcing, _" Nana, we need to have a serious conversation about Thanksgiving. You know gravy is my favorite thing, but by the time it's passed to me, it's always cold, or the gravy boat needs refilling._ _" So I have a plan. If I give you my allowance, would you go to Target and buy one of those chocolate fountains? We can plug it in and pour the gravy into it, keeping it warm and within reach at the center of the table. Everyone could have long fondue forks to dip turkey in the flowing gravy."_ How could I say no? Sooooo, we dribbled gravy across the tablecloth until the gravy got thick and clogged the fountain as we laughed our way through the holiday. The year of the gravy fountain is a treasured piece of our family history. -- Carole, North Scottsdale

## JD Vance says Jensen Huang doesn't need a pardon
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d526d4ed-6680-477d-b972-fe920daab8ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
JD Vance was at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base Wednesday and dismissed the idea that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang would need a presidential pardon. The Washington Post also reported that Pentagon officials had considered using the **Defense Production Act** to pressure Nvidia to bring Huang back. That was an idea officials reportedly discussed. There's no indication they invoked it to reinstate him.
I keep coming back to how early we are in figuring out what AI actually does in people's lives. I remember my seventh-grade English teacher coming in one day absolutely stoked because she had the internet at home. She wore bright colors, big earrings, had the crazy hair, and she couldn't wait to tell us what this thing was going to do. She said someday we'd order groceries on the internet and they'd show up at our house. We were like, what even is a website?
And then it happened. It took years to become an ordinary thing people did, and a lot of what changed would've been hard to explain to a room full of seventh-graders. For better and for worse. I think that's where we are with AI. The market is fickle because people are making enormous bets on a future they can't see clearly yet. And right now, whether one guy has a job at Nvidia can move an awful lot of money.

## If Meta wants to build a data center, Meta can pay for it

Democratic Sen. Kent Smith and Republican Sen. Louis Blessing III are sponsoring **SB 374** , which would end Ohio's authority to grant new sales and use tax exemptions for qualifying data centers. Gov. Mike DeWine already paused consideration of new requests. This would put the prohibition into law.
I'm for it. I'm fine with data centers being built here. If Meta wants to come in and build one, great. You can afford it. We have a workforce, infrastructure, resources, and a location that might make sense for your business. Those are reasons to come to Ohio. I don't see why the people who live here need to pick up part of the bill, too.
If the answer is they'll go to another state, okay. Then that state offers zero taxes. We offer zero taxes. Somebody else says, "We'll give you zero taxes and pay you to come here." How long are we supposed to play that game? Build a state where people actually want to live and businesses want to hire. There are better ways to compete than trying to be the lowest bidder every time a giant company wants to build something.
I think the same thing when I see tax breaks attached to development after development. What about the person who's lived in the same house for 50 years? They raised their kids there. Their grandkids come over. Their taxes just went up. They don't get to go down to City Hall and say, "Give me a better deal or I'm moving to Indiana." I understand why people are pissed about it.

The Army carried out a controlled detonation Wednesday to dispose of nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. ## Elon Musk says kids are getting SpaceX stock. I'll believe it when it shows up.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a67bd08a-5b21-4f0e-a878-0b5d213647ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
SpaceX says it intends to put one newly issued Class A share into each currently active Trump Account, and Elon Musk says he'll match it from his own holdings. The pledge has been valued at roughly **$18 billion**. SpaceX's contribution is expected first. Musk says his shares will transfer when his lockup expires in **June 2027**.
My issue with Elon is whether I can trust what he says he'll deliver. The guy has done extraordinary things in American industry. I can give him credit for that and still remember the Cybertruck promises about price and range, or how long people with Roadster deposits have been waiting. I appreciate that somebody made a truck that didn't look like every other vehicle on the road. I still thought the thing was a letdown.
I bought a 2021 Tesla Model Y with Full Self-Driving. At the time, to me it was glorified cruise control. It got better. I still bought something called Full Self-Driving and spent years wondering if the hardware in my car would ever do what I thought I'd paid for. So if the SpaceX share shows up in your child's account, great. Look at what actually landed and what rights come with it. Then see whether Musk's match shows up in June.
I like the idea behind these accounts. Eligible children born from **January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2028** can qualify for a **one-time $1,000 federal contribution**. Most private contributions are generally subject to a **$5,000 annual limit**. Give a kid a chance to start adult life with something set aside. I know Democrats who've taken advantage of it. I don't hear nearly enough Democrats talking about why it's a good idea. I think we ought to be able to say so even if Trump put his name on it.
