Already subscribed? Set it up on or . Good morning, my fellow Angry Democrats. Happy Thanksgiving. I hope you woke up a little less stressed today. Maybe you're making pies, maybe you're getting ready to go somewhere, or maybe you're staying home to watch football. Whatever you're doing, I hope it's a good day. Thanksgiving has always been my favorite holiday. My dad is still a pastor, and we grew up Christian, but we didn't celebrate Christmas or Easter. We observed holidays like Passover, and we celebrated the Fourth of July and Thanksgiving. Thanksgiving was the one where Mom would get up early and cook for everybody. My uncle and grandpa would come over, watch football, and drink beer. Mom had the little hors d'oeuvres out and really got that whole autumn feeling going. Sometimes we'd do it at Grandma's. Either way, it was the holiday I remember getting the family together. Today we're going to my cousin's house. They had a baby about five months ago, so we're going to see how that little one is doing. Before I go, we've got an Ohio bill to end new data center tax breaks, a SpaceX pledge I'll believe when the shares show up, and a question about what Democrats think voters just sent them to Washington to do. | | ---|---|--- Today's Government Watch List All times are Eastern. Cuyahoga County offices are closed for Thanksgiving. Monday, November 30, at 9:30 a.m. | Cleveland Health, Human Services and the Arts Committee operational review. Monday, November 30, at 10 a.m. | Cuyahoga County Community Development & Housing Committee. Monday, November 30, at 1 p.m. | Cuyahoga County Council budget hearing. Monday, November 30, at 2 p.m. | Cleveland Finance, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee. Monday, November 30, at 7 p.m. | Cleveland City Council regular meeting. Tuesday, December 1, at 10 a.m. | Cuyahoga County Human Resources, Appointments & Equity Committee. Tuesday, December 1, at 3 p.m. | Cuyahoga County Council Operations, Information Technology & Public Transportation Committee. If you've never put a council livestream on in the background like a podcast, you can. Check the meeting listings for viewing details. Chris Van Hollen picks up another endorsement against Chuck Schumer | | ---|---|--- Maine Sen.-elect Troy Jackson endorsed Chris Van Hollen on Wednesday in the race for Senate Democratic leader. Jackson backs eliminating the filibuster, Medicare for All, and raising the federal minimum wage. I'm watching this for what it tells us about what senators want the caucus to do once it takes over. JD Vance says Jensen Huang doesn't need a pardon | | ---|---|--- JD Vance was at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base Wednesday and dismissed the idea that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang would need a presidential pardon. The Washington Post also reported that Pentagon officials had considered using the Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia to bring Huang back. That was an idea officials reportedly discussed. There's no indication they invoked it to reinstate him. I keep coming back to how early we are in figuring out what AI actually does in people's lives. I remember my seventh-grade English teacher coming in one day absolutely stoked because she had the internet at home. She wore bright colors, big earrings, had the crazy hair, and she couldn't wait to tell us what this thing was going to do. She said someday we'd order groceries on the internet and they'd show up at our house. We were like, what even is a website? And then it happened. It took years to become an ordinary thing people did, and a lot of what changed would've been hard to explain to a room full of seventh-graders. For better and for worse. I think that's where we are with AI. The market is fickle because people are making enormous bets on a future they can't see clearly yet. And right now, whether one guy has a job at Nvidia can move an awful lot of money. The Rooster and what's left of local news | | ---|---|--- put out a column Wednesday called "Is Columbus a militant city?" Go check it out. Everybody knows The Rooster has its own way of covering politics. I'm glad somebody down there is willing to do it. I used to deliver a little local paper. I think it was the Sun. Those papers told you who won the high school football game or what was opening down the street. West Life is still doing local reporting in parts of the west side. In other places, it's hit or miss. A lot of the papers that used to do this either disappeared or don't have the people to cover what they once did. So now some guy with the audacity to sit down and make a podcast or write an article is part of how you find out what's happening in your own community. D.J. does a hell of a job covering politics. There's still a lot going on that somebody ought to cover. Thanks, D.J., for doing what you do. Cleveland reports suspected payroll fraud to the state auditor Cleveland says it referred potential fraud involving employee timekeeping and pay to the Ohio Auditor of State. The city hasn't disclosed how much money might be involved. What we have right now is a referral involving suspected irregularities. I want to see what the auditor finds. Cleveland is still fighting over how to fill its police commission seats Cleveland City Council's Mayor's Appointments Committee interviewed four more Community Police Commission candidates Tuesday. Council and Mayor Justin Bibb's administration still disagree about who has appointment authority under the city charter. I've seen proposals where everybody likes the idea and nobody can tell you how it'll work on a Tuesday afternoon when two people disagree. I remember a proposal here in Cleveland about letting residents decide how to spend some public money. My questions were who oversees it, who makes the decisions, and what happens when there's a dispute. "We'll give you the money and figure it out" didn't do it for me. I haven't sat on Council. I'm sure somebody will tell me I don't know shit about how they read the charter. Fine. I'd still like somebody to show me where it says who gets to make the appointment and what happens when the mayor and Council disagree. Cleveland City Council tables the Saucy Pint loan Council voted 13 -0 Monday to table a proposed loan involving Saucy Pint House 2. Residents raised concerns about stadium and surveillance spending. The meeting also touched on the proposed $27 million modular housing factory on Central Avenue , which developers say would create 120 union jobs. MetroHealth gets $2.9 million for opioid prevention and treatment MetroHealth received a four-year, $2.9 million federal grant to oversee an expansion of opioid prevention and treatment. That's a good thing. I want to see what it means for people who need treatment and where they'll be able to get it. Bill Reineke and Beth Liston will lead their Ohio Senate caucuses Republican Bill Reineke of Tiffin is set to become Ohio Senate president. Democrat Beth Liston of Dublin will become Senate minority leader. The new General Assembly convenes in January. Ohio manufacturers want Amy Acton to shake up utility regulation The Ohio Manufacturers' Association is asking Gov.-elect Amy Acton to rethink the makeup and direction of the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio. The group says utilities have had too much influence and wants electricity customers, including businesses that use a lot of power, to have more of a voice. If Meta wants to build a data center, Meta can pay for it | | ---|---|--- Democratic Sen. Kent Smith and Republican Sen. Louis Blessing III are sponsoring SB 374 , which would end Ohio's authority to grant new sales and use tax exemptions for qualifying data centers. Gov. Mike DeWine already paused consideration of new requests. This would put the prohibition into law. I'm for it. I'm fine with data centers being built here. If Meta wants to come in and build one, great. You can afford it. We have a workforce, infrastructure, resources, and a location that might make sense for your business. Those are reasons to come to Ohio. I don't see why the people who live here need to pick up part of the bill, too. If the answer is they'll go to another state, okay. Then that state offers zero taxes. We offer zero taxes. Somebody else says, "We'll give you zero taxes and pay you to come here." How long are we supposed to play that game? Build a state where people actually want to live and businesses want to hire. There are better ways to compete than trying to be the lowest bidder every time a giant company wants to build something. I think the same thing when I see tax breaks attached to development after development. What about the person who's lived in the same house for 50 years? They raised their kids there. Their grandkids come over. Their taxes just went up. They don't get to go down to City Hall and say, "Give me a better deal or I'm moving to Indiana." I understand why people are pissed about it. Hillsdale schools say they're owed $40 million in pipeline taxes | | ---|---|--- Hillsdale Local Schools in Ashland County estimates it's owed roughly $40 million in delinquent property taxes tied to the Rover Pipeline. The pipeline crosses 18 Ohio counties, and its owners have repeatedly challenged the valuations used to calculate what they owe. Forty million dollars is the district's estimate. The valuation disputes are part of why the money is still in question. The Army destroyed the unstable stockpile in Iowa. Keep watching the test results. | | ---|---|--- The Army carried out a controlled detonation Wednesday to dispose of nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The EPA collected more than 1,200 air, land, and water samples before the operation. Its initial air monitoring afterward found no detectable airborne lead. Soil and water testing still matter. This was all over my feeds. People were sending me messages saying there'd be fallout all the way to Florida. Come on. From what I read, the Army was between a rock and a hard place. I still want to know why it took this long to deal with it and why it ended up happening right before Thanksgiving. Based on those first air results, I'll give them credit for how they handled it. Would they have taken all those precautions if nobody had been watching? I don't know. I'm skeptical. Some of what went around online was ridiculous, and I'm still glad people paid enough attention to ask what was being done and how we'd know if it worked. Elon Musk says kids are getting SpaceX stock. I'll believe it when it shows up. | | ---|---|--- SpaceX says it intends to put one newly issued Class A share into each currently active Trump Account, and Elon Musk says he'll match it from his own holdings. The pledge has been valued at roughly $18 billion. SpaceX's contribution is expected first. Musk says his shares will transfer when his lockup expires in June 2027. My issue with Elon is whether I can trust what he says he'll deliver. The guy has done extraordinary things in American industry. I can give him credit for that and still remember the Cybertruck promises about price and range, or how long people with Roadster deposits have been waiting. I appreciate that somebody made a truck that didn't look like every other vehicle on the road. I still thought the thing was a letdown. I bought a 2021 Tesla Model Y with Full Self-Driving. At the time, to me it was glorified cruise control. It got better. I still bought something called Full Self-Driving and spent years wondering if the hardware in my car would ever do what I thought I'd paid for. So if the SpaceX share shows up in your child's account, great. Look at what actually landed and what rights come with it. Then see whether Musk's match shows up in June. I like the idea behind these accounts. Eligible children born from January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2028 can qualify for a one-time $1,000 federal contribution. Most private contributions are generally subject to a $5,000 annual limit. Give a kid a chance to start adult life with something set aside. I know Democrats who've taken advantage of it. I don't hear nearly enough Democrats talking about why it's a good idea. I think we ought to be able to say so even if Trump put his name on it. Hakeem Jeffries has a list. What's the mandate? | | ---|---|--- Hakeem Jeffries told MeidasTouch that Congress should move to end the Iran war within his first 100 hours. He also talked about reversing Medicaid and SNAP cuts, restoring expanded ACA tax credits, addressing Trump's tariffs, protecting DACA recipients, and advancing the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. I want people to get their healthcare and food assistance back. If Democrats get that done, people will feel it and they'll give the party some credit. What I want to know is what happens after that. Somebody takes something from you and then gives it back. You're glad to have it. A couple of years later, you're still going to ask what they did to make your life better in the first place. I don't have a lot of confidence in Jeffries. He knows how to navigate Washington. I don't think he's a particularly good communicator, and I haven't heard enough from him to tell me where he wants to take the party after it spends time reversing Trump's cuts. I'm writing more about this because I think the mandate has been pretty consistent for the last decade. Voters keep handing it from Republicans to Democrats and back again. They want things they can afford and a government that responds to them. Democrats hear that and assume voters signed off on whatever Democrats already wanted to do. I think they ought to spend more time asking what brought voters back to them and what would make those people stay. Thanksgiving dinner costs $58.63 for ten The American Farm Bureau Federation puts its Thanksgiving dinner basket for ten at $58.63 this year. It was $48.91 in 2019 and $64.05 in 2022. So dinner costs more than it did last year and before the pandemic. It's still cheaper than it was at the 2022 peak. If somebody wants to argue at the table about whether prices are up or down, ask them what year they're comparing it to. That was a long Thanksgiving podcast. I hope you have a great day. I'll see you Friday. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by supporting Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

| | Patriot, Today is all about taking time to pause, enjoy a good meal, and appreciate the countless blessings of faith, family, and good neighbors. I am truly grateful for the incredible people across South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District who make Grand Strand and Pee Dee such a special place to call home, _and I am deeply humbled every day by the opportunity to represent you._ I also want to extend my heartfelt thanks and prayers to our brave service members, first responders, and healthcare workers spending the holiday away from their loved ones to keep our communities safe. **May your home be filled with warmth, happiness, and peace today and throughout the holiday season.** From my family to yours, **Happy Thanksgiving!**

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

We’re about to get started on tonight’s dinner, but I wanted to take a quick moment before the chaos in the kitchen begins to say: **Thank you.** I have a lot to be grateful for — my family, friends, my community — but this year especially, I am grateful for you. # The Fastest Way to Type Numbers on an iPhone
It would be convenient if Apple added a numbers row to the standard iPhone keyboard, but it hasn't happened yet. If you want an iPhone keyboard with numbers, here's how to access iOS keyboard symbols and numbers without leaving the standard keyboard.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Learn how to find the iPhone keyboard with numbers and symbols without having to switch to a different keyboard.**
* **Impress your friends with your iPhone keyboard-shortcut knowledge.**
* **To open the iPhone keyboard number row, just touch and hold the 123 button, type whatever numbers and symbols you need, then release the 123 button.**

## Find the iPhone Keyboard with Numbers in One Simple Step
### System Requirements
_While the steps below work on previous software versions, the screenshots shown were captured on an iPhone 18 Pro using iOS 27.2.__Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-17273-262521-8941774-f34ebcf49f-fp7dbc5378)._
Is a keyboard for iPhone with numbers and letters too much to ask for? Actually, it's already on your iPhone! Here's how to access numbers and symbols without leaving the ABC keyboard on your iPhone. Just open any app where you want to use a keypad with numbers, such as Messages or Notes, then:
1. Touch and hold the **123 button** to bring up the keypad with numbers. Since the button is on the left side of the screen, it works best to do this with your left hand. You'll need to keep holding it while you type the numbers and/or symbols.

---
2. While still holding the 123 button, type the numbers or symbols you need using your other hand.

name: Steve Kerrigan
subject: Happy Thanksgiving
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee Massachusetts Democratic Party
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Peter, This week, as we gather with family and friends, I want to pause and say thank you. Massachusetts Democrats don't win by accident. We won on Election Day because thousands of people decided to build something and then showed up for it, again and again. Nobody handed us that. You made it. So here’s what I’m thankful for. **I’m thankful for the volunteers** who knocked on doors in the cold, made calls after a full day of work, and kept going when the doors stayed shut. Every conversation counted, and so did every one of you. **I’m thankful for our local town committees, activists and organizers** , who do the unglamorous work all year: the meetings, the mailings, the caucuses, the sign-waving on the street corner. This movement runs on your effort in every city and town from Provincetown to Pittsfield. **I’m thankful for our donors** , who gave what they could, whether it was $5 or $500. Those contributions help us to power this movement and engage with every voter, regardless of party affiliation. **I’m thankful for the candidates and public servants** who stepped up, ran with integrity, and will continue working for Massachusetts families. **And I’m thankful for our neighbors** , the voters who listened, asked hard questions, and trusted us with their vote. We don't take that trust lightly, and we will keep earning it. The election may be over, but the work of the next one has already begun. We'll do it the same way we did this one: neighbor by neighbor and door by door. There will be new voters to meet, new organizers to train, and new communities to listen to. We can't do any of it without you. For now, I hope you take a well-earned break. Enjoy the table, the people around it, and the knowledge that you helped build something that matters. Thank you, from all of us at the Massachusetts Democratic Party. Happy Thanksgiving. With gratitude,

| | | Happy Thanksgiving, Virginia! 🦃
---
I’m grateful to have my daughters at home with my husband and me, and I’m grateful to be spending this day with my sisters, parents, and in-laws.
Thanksgiving is an opportunity for all of us to slow down and spend time with the people we love. It's also a chance to be grateful for our neighbors — for the teachers, nurses, farmers, first responders, and service members — who keep us safe and keep our communities running, including the many who will be working this holiday so the rest of us can be home.
I’m grateful to serve at this moment in time, and I'm grateful for you.
From my family to yours, we're wishing everyone a joyous, safe, and restful Thanksgiving.
Governor Abigail Spanberger

Peter,
Gratitude is essential. It gives us strength in difficult times and guides us in our service to others.
This Thanksgiving, I’m grateful for the people who look out for their neighbors and give their time and energy to making our communities stronger. That care for one another is at the heart of the movement we’ve built together.
There is so much to be thankful for after this year’s election. Our victory belongs to everyone who believes we can bring out the best in one another, overcome difficult challenges, and make the world a better place. Thank you for everything you did to move us closer to that future.
It’s an honor to stand by your side in this work, and I’m looking forward to all we can accomplish in the year ahead.
Happy Thanksgiving to you and your loved ones.
With gratitude,
Keith Ellison

Peter, today is Thanksgiving – and before you sit at the table with your loved ones, I just want to take a moment to say thank you.
**Three weeks ago** , you helped me win my seat in TX-33.
**Three weeks ago** , you helped us prove that the fight for progress is as strong as ever, even in a state like Texas.
**Three weeks ago** , you were a part of a massive blue wave that ultimately helped us flip both the House a _nd_ the Senate.
Every conversation you had with a neighbor, every door you knocked, every phone call you made, and every grassroots contribution you chipped in powered a movement that refused to back down. And I could not be more grateful for your support.
**I am so thankful that, starting in January, we will finally have a Congress willing to fight for the working people of this country and North Texas.**
Growing up here, raised by a single mom who taught in our public schools, I learned early on that nothing worthwhile is ever accomplished alone. It takes a community coming together, having each other's backs, and refusing to give up on the promise of a better future.
You showed up when it mattered most. Now, I cannot wait to get back to Washington, roll up my sleeves, and get to work for you and your family.
From the bottom of my heart, _thank you._
– Colin Allred

Dear Peter, As Billy, Shelby, Sabrina, and I gather for Thanksgiving, I’m thinking about how grateful I am for our family, and for this country we all call home. I’m thinking about my grandfathers, who fought in World War II, and the responsibility we carry to protect the democracy their generation sacrificed so much to defend. Their service reminds me that what we cherish requires something from each of us. This year, I’m especially thankful for all of you who answered that call. The historic wins we saw this November were built by people like you who refused to give up on Tennessee. People who knocked doors, made calls, and chipped in what they could. County chairs, candidates, volunteers, donors, and voters who believed our communities were worth fighting for, and proved it! Because of you, we flipped six State House seats and a congressional, moved Tennessee forward, and gave people something powerful to carry into the next chapter: **hope**. There is plenty of work ahead. More opportunities to turn the progress we’ve made into lasting change. And I’m so incredibly grateful we get to do that work together. But today, I hope you take a breath. Enjoy your people, and have another helping. Let yourself feel proud of what you helped build. From my family, and our entire Tennessee Democratic Party family, to yours - thank you for your heart, your grit, and your belief in what Tennessee can become. Happy Thanksgiving. We’re thankful for you. With gratitude,
Rachel Campbell
_Chair, Tennessee Democratic Party_

Hi team, As a pediatrician and a mom, Thanksgiving has always been my favorite kind of chaos. Kids underfoot, too many cooks in the kitchen, and at least one dessert that doesn’t quite turn out the way we planned. In the wake of our historic victory earlier this month, I’ve been thinking a lot about gratitude. I want you to know how deeply grateful I am for all of you. Because of you... I’ve met parents who feel less alone in this fight for their kids’ futures. I’ve talked with nurses, teachers, and veterans who still believe public service can be an honorable calling. I’ve felt, again and again, that South Carolina is ready for leaders who tell the truth and put people over politics. And I now have the privilege to serve you in the U.S. Senate. You’ve never owed me your time, your attention, or your support, but you’ve given it anyway. You’ve opened your homes, shared your stories, chipped in what you could, and reminded me why I decided to run. On Thanksgiving, I’m especially mindful of the families who don’t get a break from worry — about a medical bill, a prescription they can’t afford, or whether their child will have the same opportunities they did. Those are the families I carry with me into every conversation and every decision. I ran for U.S. Senate because I believe our kids deserve a state and country where their health, safety, and futures come before special interests and political games. I’m thankful that you believe that too. From my family to yours, I’m wishing you a peaceful Thanksgiving filled with good food, loud laughter, and at least one moment of quiet to take a deep breath and feel proud of the community you’re helping us build. With gratitude, Annie

clean_body: | You are receiving this email from Annie Andrews Campaign because you supported her in the past. If you want to unsubscribe from Annie's email list please . = Hi team, As a pediatrician and a mom, Thanksgiving has always been my favorite kind of chaos. Kids underfoot, too many cooks in the kitchen, and at least one dessert that doesn’t quite turn out the way we planned. In the wake of our historic victory earlier this month, I’ve been thinking a lot about gratitude. I want you to know how deeply grateful I am for all of you. Because of you... I’ve met parents who feel less alone in this fight for their kids’ futures. I’ve talked with nurses, teachers, and veterans who still believe public service can be an honorable calling. I’ve felt, again and again, that South Carolina is ready for leaders who tell the truth and put people over politics. And I now have the privilege to serve you in the U.S. Senate. You’ve never owed me your time, your attention, or your support, but you’ve given it anyway. You’ve opened your homes, shared your stories, chipped in what you could, and reminded me why I decided to run. On Thanksgiving, I’m especially mindful of the families who don’t get a break from worry — about a medical bill, a prescription they can’t afford, or whether their child will have the same opportunities they did. Those are the families I carry with me into every conversation and every decision. I ran for U.S. Senate because I believe our kids deserve a state and country where their health, safety, and futures come before special interests and political games. I’m thankful that you believe that too. From my family to yours, I’m wishing you a peaceful Thanksgiving filled with good food, loud laughter, and at least one moment of quiet to take a deep breath and feel proud of the community you’re helping us build. With gratitude, Annie | | = I'm Senator-elect Dr. Annie Andrews – I'm a mom, a pediatrician and I'm honored to serve as South Carolina's Senator. name: Citizens Alliance New Hampshire
subject: Grateful to Be in This Fight With You!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire, Dan Gray, Treasurer, 45 Lafayette Rd
body:
This has been a tough year for conservatives and for the New Hampshire values we share...

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/mIESlgWrNbZ?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | | | | | Peter,

**This has been a tough year for conservatives and for the New Hampshire values we share...**

The election results stung, the path forward in Concord looks steeper than we hoped, and the news cycle never seems to slow down.

Even so, this Thanksgiving, we find ourselves deeply grateful to be in this fight alongside you.

**We are grateful for the volunteers and paid staffers** who spent months knocking doors because they believe New Hampshire can become a true Liberty State. Their willingness to show up day after day, in all kinds of weather, kept our message moving when it mattered most.

**We are grateful to our donors** , whose support makes every single thing we do as an organization possible. Without that foundation, none of the door-knocking, texting, or outreach would have happened.

**We are grateful for everyone** who helps amplify our message and answers our calls to action. Those responses turn good intentions into real pressure on the issues that matter.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/bMRy9WCxuwy?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | **Among the bright spots this year, we managed to get 50 Pledge Signers elected to the New Hampshire House.**

Those wins matter because they give us voices in Concord who have put their commitment to limited government, parental rights, and constitutional freedom in writing.

We are not going to pretend the road ahead looks easy... We have an uphill battle in 2027.

**At the same time, there is no one we would rather be on the front lines with than you. **

Your consistency and belief in limited government, parental rights, and constitutional freedom give us reason to keep going.

This Thanksgiving, we hope you will step away from the constant news cycle and endless algorithms. Spend real time with friends, family, and loved ones.

Rest, eat well, and remember why these fights matter in the first place. The work will still be here when you get back. For now, enjoy the people around your table.

**Have a Happy and Blessed Thanksgiving from all of us at Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire!**
---

body:
Thank you for everything you’ve done to defend democracy.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144089957/662382841/-453679381?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYwODFiMzE3LWFhZTktZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzE5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=XyeLTgLlMvaaCtS-rvnG5PfmSrWID4CKy8310OjaCNY=&emci=eb9c7703-4be8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=f081b317-aae9-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=8431045)

_Formerly All On The Line_

Happy Thanksgiving, Peter — I hope you’re enjoying plenty of time with friends and loved ones (and all your favorite dishes), so I’ll keep this short.
It’s hard not to reflect on what we just went through together. And this will be a hard year to forget.
Extreme politicians tried to change the rules, draw new maps, and lock themselves into power. We faced a momentous setback in April as the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, enabling states to enact Jim Crow–style map manipulations that would erase representation for communities of color.
It could have broken democracy as we know it. Instead, we saw voters, volunteers, and people like you step up and heroically defend free and fair elections.
You rolled up your sleeves, got key information in the hands of voters who otherwise might not have turned out to the polls, and held the line. _**You were a critical part of the impact Redistricting Action and the fair maps movement had in defending our democracy and future. **_
This election brings big changes to Congress and state legislatures across the country — and we have ambitious plans to push forward landmark reform and restore voting rights everywhere we can.
**For now, we can't say it enough: We are thankful for you and this movement and all you've done to protect democracy this year. **
More soon.
Wishing you and yours a Happy Thanksgiving,
Biz
John Bisognano
President

Lawyer Up.
That’s what I posted on social media late on election night as the results rolled in.
My message echoes what the American people made clear on Election Day. They’re saying they want change. They are tired of the destruction and the corruption of Donald Trump and his administration.
[If holding this administration is worth even $1 to you, I hope you’ll join me by pitching in $1 or more today >>](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pcbhm_yp9wM0bNrRvdu41sBD7Yf9pbrnVKlsKaL4aKthQtHRaK5NpJuHe69h4PYLqqbip3UasLUb2IyQ4HRX3bf-mn_DrF1x7FiAWnCHTXNENtrmop2nLxTF1zl4I1kiLp9drAKkkJc1iaGDVb_uiW-v_LXK56gPZy6eY9ELia0ZfSSu_aSukytnUBimOw96kWGZQF2_XON_kgmnIq_Me9ExPzckibBw_o5-0wZYHe0Xxv_LSvRxSk-lp861GLZaqiQBaoGsyhw=&c=ttGGD0vWaGHzuOA6KLlCmq6Bih1hXifRj1pam1403JxyIcUwdxaL9g==&ch=t1KNVrhtMAJFNLNTXyiooXN90Efmk6fXSfCpt8-84CCTldA6DVcAHA==)
As Oversight Chair, I’ll be focused on four areas:
**1️⃣ We’re going to take on the Trump crime family.** The grift and corruption from this family are unprecedented in American politics.
2️⃣ **We’ll investigate DHS and the abuses of ICE.** When people are being kidnapped and detained, thrown to the ground, arms broken, that's inhumane, wrong, and the American public is sick of it.
3️⃣ **We will crack down on corporate corruption and consumer pricing.** We’ll investigate corporate donors to the White House ballroom, no-bid contracts like the Reflecting Pool, and other companies that are ripping off the American public.
4️⃣**We’ll get to the bottom of the Epstein Case.** We’ll pursue accountability and justice for survivors and focus on transparency, regardless of wealth, power, or political affiliation.
So if you took part in any of these crimes against the American people, my message is simple: Lawyer Up.
The American people made their choice, and they rejected Trump’s corruption. But taking on this apparatus takes resources, grit, and grassroots power.
[If seeing Donald Trump held accountable is worth even $1 to you, chip in right now to fuel this fight.](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pcbhm_yp9wM0bNrRvdu41sBD7Yf9pbrnVKlsKaL4aKthQtHRaK5NpJuHe69h4PYLqqbip3UasLUb2IyQ4HRX3bf-mn_DrF1x7FiAWnCHTXNENtrmop2nLxTF1zl4I1kiLp9drAKkkJc1iaGDVb_uiW-v_LXK56gPZy6eY9ELia0ZfSSu_aSukytnUBimOw96kWGZQF2_XON_kgmnIq_Me9ExPzckibBw_o5-0wZYHe0Xxv_LSvRxSoPkbzBKDwEGPmZCULP0sfE=&c=ttGGD0vWaGHzuOA6KLlCmq6Bih1hXifRj1pam1403JxyIcUwdxaL9g==&ch=t1KNVrhtMAJFNLNTXyiooXN90Efmk6fXSfCpt8-84CCTldA6DVcAHA==)

**We really could not have done it without you.**
You’ve shown up for us time and time again, and we’re thrilled to be going into 2027 with you standing with us.
Every donation made, deadline hit, and goal reached allowed us to help power David Crowley to victory, and we are so grateful to be welcoming David as Wisconsin’s next governor!
We hope you’re able to take time today to rest, spend time with loved ones, and proudly reflect on all of your hard work these past few months!
— Battleground Wisconsin

name: Josh
subject: From my family to yours
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOSH GOTTHEIMER FOR CONGRESS
body:
---
| | Hi team,

As we sit down with our families today, I wanted to reach out directly and wish you and your loved ones a very Happy Thanksgiving.

Most of all, I am thankful for you.

Josh Gottheimer

name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: So much to be thankful for
body:
And I am especially thankful for you
---
| | | | | |
---
This Thanksgiving, as we gather with friends and family, we have time to reflect on all we are grateful for and to share that gratitude with the people who matter most. I want to take a moment to let you know how grateful I am for you, and for your generosity, friendship, and continued support.
I’m grateful to so many friends and supporters, near and far, who joined together over the last two years to support this campaign and Democratic candidates across Texas and across the country. So many people were part of this team, giving their time, money, and energy to get out the vote. You made phone calls, wrote postcards, knocked on doors, and showed up everywhere to make a difference.
And we did. We didn’t just make a difference. We made history! We achieved what Texans have been dreaming of and working for for more than 30 years.
And the history-makers we elected, are going to make policy and laws that reflect our values and our commitment to our communities and our country.
This Thanksgiving day, I am so grateful for all of those who believed, who worked, and who refused to give up on our fellow Texans and fellow Americans.
With that in mind, and with gratitude in my heart, I wish you and your loved ones a wonderful day of Thanksgiving.
Together, we can do anything,

body:
This is the photo of a good Christian man.

Eddie needs your help..
| | | | Dear Patriot, This is the photo of a good Christian man. A loving husband of almost 20 years, a supportive father of seven, and a dedicated law enforcement officer.
---
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckcuK2zAUhp9G3jlIR74uvMhgqwwkpaTDdCmOpeNEqWQbWZ7Sty8JnReY7c93Lh__r7M-o_Nuvn7HQF1Mk46bTjcanaXZLveIzscFLdnw97Zr4FDlQuRQaTTJfZAuMLOdNRaFyagTdVvWvOayyW4doWkIWxyhBmgaGEcxtc1kJYlmqk2Zue6xTwioRCm5rA4t8LKpBY1FSRwNsIKjp5gOkdZ99M7gnHD7PS3R0MEsIfPdLaV1Y_LIQDFQG5k90gFnskt6EAyUJ28nBmpFUbVFnQtR8by4h7somVR7Cnpb9miIyf4yvDOoHlEg6_bAZD-cj6-n_6HBsKK7zkz2z8c5CP3Sf9On4dQrfRne9ZPWw_nlFX7mP4755U19zi5zojk9jryp_NM7i51d_zjv3VbVrODXgM4_zdIXy_jo4F8AAAD__zJelZ0)
---
I'm proud to call former Jal, New Mexico Police Officer Eddie Embly my husband... **[...and I'm urgently asking you to help keep him from spending the next decade in federal prison.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckcuK2zAUhp9G3jlIR74uvMhgqwwkpaTDdCmOpeNEqWQbWZ7Sty8JnReY7c93Lh__r7M-o_Nuvn7HQF1Mk46bTjcanaXZLveIzscFLdnw97Zr4FDlQuRQaTTJfZAuMLOdNRaFyagTdVvWvOayyW4doWkIWxyhBmgaGEcxtc1kJYlmqk2Zue6xTwioRCm5rA4t8LKpBY1FSRwNsIKjp5gOkdZ99M7gnHD7PS3R0MEsIfPdLaV1Y_LIQDFQG5k90gFnskt6EAyUJ28nBmpFUbVFnQtR8by4h7somVR7Cnpb9miIyf4yvDOoHlEg6_bAZD-cj6-n_6HBsKK7zkz2z8c5CP3Sf9On4dQrfRne9ZPWw_nlFX7mP4755U19zi5zojk9jryp_NM7i51d_zjv3VbVrODXgM4_zdIXy_jo4F8AAAD__zJelZ0)** Please, allow me to explain... In July 2021, my husband responded to a call about a suspicious vehicle at a local truck stop. The driver was disoriented, sweating, unsteady, and acting erratically. Officers had to use a Taser to take him into custody.My husband had a limited role in the arrest - he helped move the suspect to the patrol car and transported him a short distance to the police station. Shortly after arriving at the station, the suspect became unresponsive and was pronounced dead. After investigating, the state medical examiner definitively ruled the cause of death as methamphetamine toxicity. So imagine our shock when over two years later, the Biden Department of Justice accused Eddie of "failing to intervene" and a "deliberate indifference to medical needs" - and charged him under a federal civil rights statute carrying up to 20 years in prison. We poured our life savings into Eddie's defense, expecting justice would prevail at trial and he'd soon be back on the job. But instead, the government blocked all evidence of the suspect's meth overdose from the trial.**The jury found Eddie GUILTY - and he faces up to 20 years in prison.** Now Eddie will miss graduations and birthdays. He won't get to walk our daughters down the aisle.And he'll miss the birth of future grandchildren.With nowhere to turn, I turned to God and prayed like I've never prayed before...And God answered our prayers - in the form of a phone call from Jason Johnson with the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). For the first time in months, I see a future with Eddie by my side enjoying our golden years.But LELDF doesn't receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts are few and far between.Instead, LELDF relies on kind-hearted strangers who respect our men and women in blue and want to help cops like Eddie who are unjustly convicted.Folks, I pray, like you.**[Will you help LELDF fight for Eddie by making a tax-deductible donation of $35, $50, $100, or more today?](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckcuK2zAUhp9G3jlIR74uvMhgqwwkpaTDdCmOpeNEqWQbWZ7Sty8JnReY7c93Lh__r7M-o_Nuvn7HQF1Mk46bTjcanaXZLveIzscFLdnw97Zr4FDlQuRQaTTJfZAuMLOdNRaFyagTdVvWvOayyW4doWkIWxyhBmgaGEcxtc1kJYlmqk2Zue6xTwioRCm5rA4t8LKpBY1FSRwNsIKjp5gOkdZ99M7gnHD7PS3R0MEsIfPdLaV1Y_LIQDFQG5k90gFnskt6EAyUJ28nBmpFUbVFnQtR8by4h7somVR7Cnpb9miIyf4yvDOoHlEg6_bAZD-cj6-n_6HBsKK7zkz2z8c5CP3Sf9On4dQrfRne9ZPWw_nlFX7mP4755U19zi5zojk9jryp_NM7i51d_zjv3VbVrODXgM4_zdIXy_jo4F8AAAD__zJelZ0)** No matter how much you're able to help, your donation will be put to immediate use, helping LELDF support Eddie and a dozen other wrongly accused officers.That's why I'm asking you to help LELDF fund Eddie's appeal by making an urgent donation today.The appeal will cost approximately $175,000 - **so whether you can give $35, $50, $100, $250, $500 or more - every gift will make a huge difference.** But no matter how much you're able to send in support of Eddie, please pray for us.I know firsthand the power of prayer. ### **Help us beat and replace the mainstream media! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today:**
[ Support Our Journalism](https://substack.com/redirect/7ac5dda9-7038-42d0-83b7-893fdd453df3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Most of us have a fairly extensive list of things we would like God to straighten out this Thanksgiving. I certainly do. There are prayers I would love answered, problems I would happily retire, and a prolonged lesson in spiritual warfare I would never have voluntarily enrolled in. I have offered the Lord some very specific suggestions. He has yet to put me in charge.
Then I think about the people we remember today. They crossed an ocean in a wooden ship, endured a brutal first winter, buried people they loved, and began building a life with no assurance it would succeed.
We have reduced them to buckled hats and table decorations. There is a considerably better story there.
## **They Had to Board the Ship**
Among the Mayflower passengers were English Separatists whose religious convictions had brought them into conflict with the established church. They had already lived in the Netherlands before undertaking the Atlantic crossing. Other passengers came for different reasons, including economic opportunity. People with different interests were attempting something extraordinarily difficult together.
For the Separatists, faith meant making decisions about where they would live, how they would worship, and what they were willing to risk.
They had to board the ship.
They could not check the hospital ratings, consult a weather app, or book a return flight if the neighborhood disappointed them. They went with what they could carry and what they believed.
I wonder how many of us would have made it past the packing.
The first winter at Plymouth was devastating. Roughly half the Mayflower's passengers died during the first winter and its aftermath. Families lost mothers, fathers, spouses, and children. The survivors had to keep working while grieving because their survival depended on it.
By the harvest gathering of 1621, they had food and a reason to hope. They also had graves.
A successful crop could not restore the people they had buried.
## **There Was Enough to Share**
Edward Winslow, a Mayflower passenger who later became governor of Plymouth Colony, left a brief **[eyewitness account](https://substack.com/redirect/3e67534a-c362-45d1-b27d-45170169119c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of the 1621 harvest gathering. He described three days of feasting attended by Ousamequin, often called Massasoit, a leader of the Wampanoag people, whose homeland included present-day southeastern Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island. About ninety Wampanoag men joined him and contributed five deer to the gathering.
Wampanoag knowledge of the land and assistance had helped the English settlers establish themselves. Their contribution belongs in the story of that harvest and the people who shared it.
The event we now call **[the first Thanksgiving was a harvest celebration](https://substack.com/redirect/15680637-b21c-41d1-bf84-12546f667517?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. The English colonists also observed specifically religious days of thanksgiving on other occasions. Our modern holiday developed over generations.
What stays with me is what that harvest must have meant after the winter they had endured. Food meant they might survive another season. There was enough to gather, eat, and share.
They could recognize that blessing while still carrying their losses.
How often do we insist that the thing hurting us must be resolved before we can be thankful for anything else?
_**(Piece continues below):**_
* * *
# **We will not give up hope, and neither should you**
The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ac5dda9-7038-42d0-83b7-893fdd453df3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
We must fight for our nation with everything we, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
**PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..bg_fbmpHWQmaKSXx2kZPpF4sLS2jENAFMi-PIYHq-20?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=226570679)
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
_-The PolitiBrawl Editors_
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
## **Washington Gave Thanks. Lincoln Did Not Wait for Peace.**
In 1789, George Washington **[proclaimed](https://substack.com/redirect/c6bf9a08-94c6-4eb3-838f-77e415e9beb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a national day of thanksgiving and prayer for November 26. He called on Americans to acknowledge God's blessings and seek His guidance.
The practice was not yet the consistent annual observance we know today. That tradition took hold under Abraham Lincoln, who in October 1863 **[called for a national Thanksgiving](https://substack.com/redirect/88c9b47b-5627-49c4-bb72-a54e1f81d07d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on the last Thursday of November.
The country was in the middle of the Civil War.
Think about that before deciding the people at your table are too divided to get through dinner.
Lincoln was leading a nation whose divisions had become battlefields. His proclamation recognized blessings while calling for care for widows, orphans, mourners, and those suffering because of the war. He asked Americans to give thanks and seek healing while the conflict continued.
He did not wait for a united country.
There is something in that for us.
## **Can We Let It Go for a Day?**
We are coming into this Thanksgiving angry. After the midterm slaughter, some of us can barely get through a conversation without returning to politics. Families are fighting. People who love one another are forgetting how to speak to one another.
I have certainly had plenty to say. Anyone who has read my recent pieces knows that.
But can we let it go for a day?
The election results will still be there Friday. So will the arguments. You can return to holding people accountable without spending Thanksgiving cross-examining your brother-in-law over the stuffing.
Your soul needs rest. Your brain needs a break. Your family needs time with you that does not become another debate.
You do not have to abandon a single conviction to ask someone how they are doing and listen to the answer. You can disagree with your sister's politics and remember why you love her. You can put down the phone without surrendering the country.
Ask your father about his childhood. Let your mother finish the story you have heard twelve times. There may come a Thanksgiving when you would give anything to hear it a thirteenth.
Give thanks for the people sitting there while you still have them.
## **Jesus Knows About the Unfinished Business**
I am a mother and a founder. I like things that work. When there is a problem, I want to identify it, address it, and get on with building something useful. Waiting has never been my most impressive quality.
I bring that same enthusiasm to prayer. Jesus knows.
But I cannot make gratitude contingent on receiving the answer I requested, in the form I requested, by the deadline I thought was perfectly reasonable.
Sometimes I have to look past the problem occupying the entire room and notice the child standing beside me. I have to put down the phone long enough to hear the laughter. I have to recognize the friend who keeps checking in and the strength that somehow arrived when I had no idea how I would get through the day.
Those things count while the larger problem is still there.
Jesus is present in that unfinished life. He knows what hurts. I can bring Him the frustration and thank Him for sustaining me through it. Some of my most honest prayers contain both.
You do not have to pretend this has been a wonderful year to recognize the people and moments that helped you survive it.

## **Set Another Place**
Before the day gets away from you, think about who might be spending it alone.
Someone you know may have quietly decided not to make a meal because cooking for one feels unbearable. Someone may be facing a first Thanksgiving without a spouse, a parent, or a child. Someone may be surrounded by people and still be struggling.
An invitation does not have to be elaborate to matter. Neither does a phone call.
You do not need matching china to make a person feel wanted.
And once everyone sits down, be there. Put the phone away. The gravy deserves your attention, and so do the people.
Let the children hear the family stories, even the ones they roll their eyes at. These are their core memories being made around your table. Someday, they may be the ones telling those stories to their own children, remembering who told them first.
Tell someone what their presence in your life has meant. If a person is missing this year, say their name if you can. A few tears do not ruin Thanksgiving.
I love the beautiful table, the food, and the traditions. I intend to enjoy all of them. There is no spiritual prize for pretending pumpkin pie is unimportant.
But the people come first.
The survivors at Plymouth had endured a terrible year. Washington asked a new nation to acknowledge its blessings. Lincoln called a divided country to give thanks while war still raged.
We can bring our unfinished business to the table and leave it alone long enough to recognize what God has placed in front of us.
Hold your children close. Call your mother. Thank the person who stood beside you when you were difficult to stand beside. Feed somebody.
And thank Jesus for carrying you this far.
We can keep praying about what comes next.

Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: Most of us have a fairly extensive list of things we would like God to straighten out this Thanksgiving. I certainly do. There are prayers I would love answered, problems I would happily retire, and a prolonged lesson in spiritual warfare I would never have voluntarily enrolled in. I have offered the Lord some very specific suggestions. He has yet to put me in charge. Then I think about the people we remember today. They crossed an ocean in a wooden ship, endured a brutal first winter, buried people they loved, and began building a life with no assurance it would succeed. We have reduced them to buckled hats and table decorations. There is a considerably better story there. They Had to Board the Ship Among the Mayflower passengers were English Separatists whose religious convictions had brought them into conflict with the established church. They had already lived in the Netherlands before undertaking the Atlantic crossing. Other passengers came for different reasons, including economic opportunity. People with different interests were attempting something extraordinarily difficult together. For the Separatists, faith meant making decisions about where they would live, how they would worship, and what they were willing to risk. They had to board the ship. They could not check the hospital ratings, consult a weather app, or book a return flight if the neighborhood disappointed them. They went with what they could carry and what they believed. I wonder how many of us would have made it past the packing. The first winter at Plymouth was devastating. Roughly half the Mayflower's passengers died during the first winter and its aftermath. Families lost mothers, fathers, spouses, and children. The survivors had to keep working while grieving because their survival depended on it. By the harvest gathering of 1621, they had food and a reason to hope. They also had graves. A successful crop could not restore the people they had buried. There Was Enough to Share Edward Winslow, a Mayflower passenger who later became governor of Plymouth Colony, left a brief of the 1621 harvest gathering. He described three days of feasting attended by Ousamequin, often called Massasoit, a leader of the Wampanoag people, whose homeland included present-day southeastern Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island. About ninety Wampanoag men joined him and contributed five deer to the gathering. Wampanoag knowledge of the land and assistance had helped the English settlers establish themselves. Their contribution belongs in the story of that harvest and the people who shared it. The event we now call . The English colonists also observed specifically religious days of thanksgiving on other occasions. Our modern holiday developed over generations. What stays with me is what that harvest must have meant after the winter they had endured. Food meant they might survive another season. There was enough to gather, eat, and share. They could recognize that blessing while still carrying their losses. How often do we insist that the thing hurting us must be resolved before we can be thankful for anything else? PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news. We appreciate your readership and support. Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day. -The PolitiBrawl Editors (Piece continues): Washington Gave Thanks. Lincoln Did Not Wait for Peace. In 1789, George Washington a national day of thanksgiving and prayer for November 26. He called on Americans to acknowledge God's blessings and seek His guidance. The practice was not yet the consistent annual observance we know today. That tradition took hold under Abraham Lincoln, who in October 1863 on the last Thursday of November. The country was in the middle of the Civil War. Think about that before deciding the people at your table are too divided to get through dinner. Lincoln was leading a nation whose divisions had become battlefields. His proclamation recognized blessings while calling for care for widows, orphans, mourners, and those suffering because of the war. He asked Americans to give thanks and seek healing while the conflict continued. He did not wait for a united country. There is something in that for us. Can We Let It Go for a Day? We are coming into this Thanksgiving angry. After the midterm slaughter, some of us can barely get through a conversation without returning to politics. Families are fighting. People who love one another are forgetting how to speak to one another. I have certainly had plenty to say. Anyone who has read my recent pieces knows that. But can we let it go for a day? name: Helen Gym
subject: Giving thanks
body:
What you made possible this year
| |
---
| Hi Peter, As many of us prepare to gather with family and loved ones, our team is reflecting on what we’re most grateful for this year: you, and the power of our communities coming together for one another. Recently, one of our team members Nina shared a moment from her post-election phone bank. While making calls in Vietnamese to older community members, she heard the same sentiment over and over: this year they wanted their vote to count. They want a change in the direction of our country. Their vote was their voice, and together our voices were heard loud and clear on Election Day. On this holiday, here’s what we are thankful for:
# **A Change Election and AAPI Power**
****_[Refugee and immigrant residents educated and engaged voters who threw out an anti-immigrant Congressman. Photo: API PA]_ This year, API PA built the largest multilingual field program in the Commonwealth. Alongside partners like Seed the Vote and CAIR, we knocked on 100,000 doors, made 3 million calls across 22 languages, and had 50,000 direct conversations with AAPI voters. We trained 200 people as Democracy Defenders and staffed our multilingual Voter Protection Hotline so every voter knew their rights and had their ballot counted. That grassroots power helped flip critical seats in Congress such as PA-01 (electing Bob Harvie) and PA-10 (defeating Scott Perry), as well as a critical state senate seat (electing Eileen Abillar) that helped deliver Pennsylvania’s first Democratic trifecta in over 30 years.

We also made over 800,000 calls to support AAPI partner organizations who won federal and state races across Texas, North Carolina, and Arizona.
# **ICE OUT everywhere**
_[API PA joined with Asian Americans United and National Domestic Workers Alliance to call for an end to ICE practices at the Philadelphia International Airport. Photo: Joe Piette]_ We’re organizing for a future where everyone can live with safety, dignity, and without the fear of ICE violence. In Philadelphia, we joined the ICE OUT PHL Coalition at the Philadelphia International Airport to demand City and airport officials do everything in their power to end the ICE presence that has been terrorizing travellers. Since July, at least 50 people have been detained at the airport while travelling or working. The airport should be a place where people can travel safely, not a place where families fear being detained, separated, and suddenly in ICE custody. In Dauphin County, we’re working with our partners to pass a Welcoming County Resolution at the County Commission and end ICE collaboration at the Dauphin County prisons, where at least one individual died after being transferred to ICE custody. County resources must be used to serve and protect residents – not facilitate immigration detention and family separation.
# **New Coalitions and Partners**
****_[CASA in Action, Asian Refugees United, and API PA joined together to demand an end to ICE collaboration in the Dauphin County prisons. Photo: API PA]_ The challenges facing our communities are connected, and lasting change takes all of us working together. We’re grateful for partnerships that bridge racial, ethnic, and cultural communities to fight for what our communities need. API PA convenes the AAPI Power Caucus, a network of 17 statewide Asian American serving organizations working to keep immigrant and refugee communities safe all over Pennsylvania. With the PA Voters Decide coalition and Hands Off Our Votes coalition, we built a stronger democracy where all of our voices could be heard and our votes counted. With the PA Climate Equity Table and the No Data Centers in Philly Coalition we champion affordable utilities as well as a future where we all have a say in what happens in our neighborhoods.
* * *
None of this happens without you. Every conversation, every door knocked, , every phone call, every meal distributed, and every person who decides to get involved helps build the power we need to create lasting change. **You are what makes this movement possible – and we want to build what comes next with you.** Whether you’re already organizing in your neighborhood, supporting your neighbors through mutual aid, or looking to hold our newly elected leaders accountable in 2027, we’re stronger when we organize side by side. API PA is a political home built for Asian Americans in Pennsylvania. Take the next step and become an official [**member today.** ](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/TdaIPErbxonUvYOH8btgsGWRTRNwVgEy/click?signature=c2791179952cad1a8e355c54323cac51460f480a&url=http%3A%2F%2Fapipennsylvania.org%2Fmembership)The change you want to see in the world is possible when we organize together and we’re so grateful you’re choosing to be part of API PA! In gratitude, Helen Gym Interim Executive Director Asian Pacific Islander Political Alliance (API PA)

name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: This Thanksgiving, I am thankful for you
body:
Even in a difficult year, we have so much to thank God for.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/010001a21880069d-d2f7e1fe-eb39-4694-9a46-904839b9d67f-000000/SiQWki3zju4yvlrYd6HqPaEWz09dspL-W0btypbUVII=452)Patriot–As we celebrate Thanksgiving today, I want you to know that when I count my blessings, you are among them.This has been a difficult year in many ways. I know there have been disappointments, frustrations, and, for many of you, personal hardships that have nothing to do with politics. And yet, even in the midst of a difficult year, we have so much for which to thank God.In 1789, when our country was still young and its future far from certain, George Washington proclaimed a national day of thanksgiving and prayer. Among the blessings for which he called on Americans to give thanks was “the civil and religious liberty with which we are blessed.”More than two centuries later, what a gift it is that we can still give thanks for those same freedoms.I am grateful to live in this beautiful country. I am grateful for my family, my friends, and the many wonderful people God has brought into my life through the tea party movement.And I am especially thankful for you. Over the years, I have had the privilege of getting to know so many of you, hearing your stories, meeting your families, and developing friendships that I treasure. Whether we have had the opportunity to meet in person or not, please know how grateful I am to have you in my life.I hope today brings you good food, laughter, and time with the people you love. clean_body: Even in a difficult year, we have so much to thank God for. –As we celebrate Thanksgiving today, I want you to know that when I count my blessings, you are among them.This has been a difficult year in many ways. I know there have been disappointments, frustrations, and, for many of you, personal hardships that have nothing to do with politics. And yet, even in the midst of a difficult year, we have so much for which to thank God.In 1789, when our country was still young and its future far from certain, George Washington proclaimed a national day of thanksgiving and prayer. Among the blessings for which he called on Americans to give thanks was “the civil and religious liberty with which we are blessed.”More than two centuries later, what a gift it is that we can still give thanks for those same freedoms.I am grateful to live in this beautiful country. I am grateful for my family, my friends, and the many wonderful people God has brought into my life through the tea party movement.And I am especially thankful for you. Over the years, I have had the privilege of getting to know so many of you, hearing your stories, meeting your families, and developing friendships that I treasure. Whether we have had the opportunity to meet in person or not, please know how grateful I am to have you in my life.I hope today brings you good food, laughter, and time with the people you love. Peter,

From my family to yours, Happy Thanksgiving.

Seth

name: Marcy Kaptur
subject: Grateful for you
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/95655/images/kaptur-email-header-2.png]

Happy Thanksgiving, friend.

Thanksgiving is a time to reflect on the blessings of family, community, and all that we have to be grateful for. This year, I find myself especially grateful for each of you.

This year, we faced one of America’s most targeted races. Our district was redrawn to make the path forward more difficult, and outside groups spent millions trying to define our record and undermine the work we have done together.

There were plenty who counted us out. But you never wavered. You knocked on doors, made calls, sent texts, talked with your neighbors, and stepped forward when it mattered most. Your commitment, generosity, and belief in what we are working to accomplish made all the difference.

As we gather for Thanksgiving, I want you to know how deeply grateful I am for your friendship and support over the years. Your continued faith in our work is something I never take for granted. It is both a profound honor and a privilege to represent this remarkable region of Ohio and the people who make it such a special place.

Thank you for standing with me, and for always remembering that the greatest strength of any effort is the people who believe in it.

With gratitude,

Marcy
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/95655/images/kaptur-email-headshot.jpg]

About Marcy Kaptur
Marcy Kaptur is a fighter for high-wage jobs, growing a workforce to meet the needs of the 21st century, and protecting our region’s most vital natural resource, the Great Lakes. She’s worked with both parties to secure investments in our communities and has been a true friend of veterans, seniors, first responders and working people. She’s a voice for us all in the People’s House.

Happy Thanksgiving, folks! If you’re sharing the table with your family, there are bound to be discussions of politics and current events that come up. So today, we’re providing you with five easy ways to piss off your MAGA uncle while waiting for the turkey to cook.
1. Remind them that Democrats had a historic victory on Election Day, which many are seeing as an indictment of Trump, his policies, and the whole MAGA movement. I mean, we won Texas, South Carolina, Mississippi...
2. Encourage them to find a single candidate in the Republican party who could take Trump’s place and lead his coalition after 2028.
3. Remind them that Trump is solely responsible for the massive influx of volunteers that came out to work against MAGA candidates like Darren Bailey.
4. Ask them to look up the price of gas, and then explain patiently that gas prices are high because of the needless war that Trump started in Iran.
5. Say “Thank you Habibi”.

We also want to thank you for everything. We would not be as successful as we were on Election Day if it were not for your support, your passion, and your enthusiasm. Thank you for being with us in the fight for our values and the future of our country.

We do not take your trust in us and our mission lightly.

Please, enjoy this holiday with your loved ones, and just know that we’re grateful for you and everything you do.

– IDCCA

#### Liftoff, Then Gravity
## **SpaceX slips below its IPO price as the bill for its AI ambitions comes due**
_The biggest stock sale on record is turning into a lesson in what a balance sheet can do to a good story._
Our partner above is focused on Elon Musk's next move. This week, the market is busy putting a price on his most recent one.
SpaceX shares, first sold to the public at $135 in June, traded below that price all day Wednesday and were down more than 9 percent at one point before recovering most of the loss. The stock had already been through [a bruising week](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d9d80d09-1afb-461c-a678-10e663236440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), sliding about 11 percent through Tuesday.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5441e9b4-4043-4ff7-a205-093c3d739b72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The worry is money. SpaceX sold $32 billion of debt last week to fund Nvidia chips it will lease for about five years, and most of it priced at yields above 8 percent. Its free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and building data centers, was negative $35 billion through the first nine months of the year, and the cost of [insurance against a default](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a149f799-0a37-4b75-b254-969a91a38dda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on its bonds hit a record this week.
There is a date on the calendar too. On Dec. 8, a lockup ends, freeing insiders and early backers to sell shares that have been off-limits since the June listing. The shares peaked near $225 in their first weeks of trading.
I have no quarrel with big dreams; I just want to see the cash show up before I pay up for one.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8150bb03-b69e-4925-b18e-c6ef7c8f9d57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d6403bb8-2e2b-4aea-8a1d-dfc4d0386aa9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Shoppers are about to hand the Fed fresh evidence on the economy, and our next partner is watching the central bank closely too.
#### From Our Partners
#### **[Millionaire warns: "Move your money now."](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0f22b5d7-b1ab-44a0-bec8-ea7b8b617f1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0f22b5d7-b1ab-44a0-bec8-ea7b8b617f1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Larry Benedict generated $274 million in profits for his clients by knowing where money flows when the Federal Reserve shifts.
He says Trump's Fed Takeover is triggering the most significant shift in U.S. markets in nearly 20 years.
He's already identified the one ticker he expects billions to flood into... and he's giving away the name for free.
**[Click here to get the full details before the window closes.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0f22b5d7-b1ab-44a0-bec8-ea7b8b617f1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
#### Checkout Season
### **Online holiday spending is running ahead of forecast, and more of it is on installment plans**
Americans spent more than $82.5 billion online in the first 22 days of November, up 9.1 percent from a year earlier. That outpaces the 6.7 percent growth forecast for the full season, and it stands out after a government report this week showed October spending, adjusted for prices, slipped slightly.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4381db0c-509d-4141-91d6-de32579a0ccf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* Every day this month has topped $3 billion online, and two days crossed $4 billion, the first time that has happened before Thanksgiving, according to [Adobe's running tally](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fba1e763-8533-472a-abf6-4967d626e5c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Buy now, pay later plans, which split a purchase into installments, have already carried $6.1 billion of spending, up 6.5 percent.
* Black Friday is forecast to bring in $12.9 billion online, up 9.2 percent, with the [deepest discounts of the season](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/45927860-3554-4399-a1a1-c52b7081bf41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on TVs, toys, apparel, appliances and furniture.
* Cyber Monday is still expected to be the biggest day, at $15.1 billion, with electronics and computers at their cheapest.

Installment plans feel light at the register, and the payments arrive in January alongside the credit card statement.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/11aba866-e54b-4146-a331-736594aa3e95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### One Number
**7.21%** is the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage this week, according to [Freddie Mac's latest survey](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/13536235-5e3c-4e70-85f2-b7c8799b4f0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), down from 7.28 percent a week ago. On a $400,000 loan, that works out to about $2,718 a month in principal and interest, roughly $260 more than the same loan cost at last year's rate of 6.23 percent. That is more than $3,100 a year for the same house.
#### Why I Led Here
This one rhymes with Facebook in 2012. That listing came at $38 a share, fell below half that within four months, and needed more than a year to climb back to its offer price.
What finally turned it was profits showing up on the statement, and that is the yardstick I will hold SpaceX to as well. On a day for counting blessings, I would rather own a business that sends cash home than one that keeps asking for more.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8054134d-2863-49c3-89a5-122dc79e70b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a15b2d1-a3a7-4cba-b0f2-ba3f3137f065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_When the world moves, hold your ground._

| | Dear Moms, Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at Moms for America! Today, as we count our blessings, I am especially grateful for the gift of family, the freedoms we cherish, and the incredible women across our nation who pour their hearts into their homes, families, and communities. And that includes YOU! I thank God for each of you and the privilege of walking alongside you on this journey of motherhood. Never underestimate the difference you make in the lives of your children or the generations that will follow. As you gather around your Thanksgiving table today, I encourage you to take a moment to share the story of America's first Thanksgiving with your loved ones. To help you do just that, we have a [special video ](https://momsforamerica.us/so/aeQ8OG3oi/c?w=0D9BKHFK8Ea-W33s00vGol4nGTZD5_8g85pUwHt32Gw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS93XzI0Y0dWRzcyND9zaT1aaG9IMy1oejltSDhHMXJBIiwiciI6IjQ3ZTgwYzAzLWRkZDctNDFjMi1iODk1LTdlNDczZTVjZjI2NCIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6ImIzODM4YmY4LWZhYjAtNDFiOS05NjczLWU4YzZiZWZiNjU3NyJ9)featuring Kirk Cameron from [Our American Story](https://momsforamerica.us/so/aeQ8OG3oi/c?w=lSVDW7VRuZKyhoLZYxvcsDbZU5_aVqrGfAxJIAcTamE.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vdXIyNTBzdG9yeS5jb20vIiwiciI6IjQ3ZTgwYzAzLWRkZDctNDFjMi1iODk1LTdlNDczZTVjZjI2NCIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6ImIzODM4YmY4LWZhYjAtNDFiOS05NjczLWU4YzZiZWZiNjU3NyJ9), our brand-new theatrical production created to bring America's remarkable history to life for families and communities across the nation. Watch and share the [Thanksgiving story](https://momsforamerica.us/so/aeQ8OG3oi/c?w=g6awQ5k9KgrwZRJ4tLjUywRSxgoz_7stnbiyvOtPMaU.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS93XzI0Y0dWRzcyNCIsInIiOiI0N2U4MGMwMy1kZGQ3LTQxYzItYjg5NS03ZTQ3M2U1Y2YyNjQiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) with your family. May we never take for granted the blessings God has bestowed upon us, the freedoms we have inherited, or the opportunity we have to pass that precious legacy on to our children. From my family to yours, may your Thanksgiving be filled with joy, laughter, love, and gratitude. God bless you, your family, and America! With a grateful heart,Kimberly Fletcher
Founder & President, Moms for America

Hi friend, I’m grateful for so many things this year. Time spent with family, friends, and neighbors. Working with our diverse communities, united by our shared love for Southwest Ohio. And for people like you, who haven’t given up on good governance and are willing to step up and fight for it. It’s been a rough year filled with uncertainty, but this past month has felt like finding our way back to steady ground. You’re the engine powering our vision forward: one where no one, including the president, is above the law, and where families can rest easy after a hard day’s work, knowing they can afford to care for their loved ones. I’m honored to have earned the trust of voters once more and to represent OH-01 in Washington. And I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work. But for today, I’m celebrating the renewed hope and determination you give me as we push for a better future for Southwest Ohio kids and families. From our family to yours, Happy Thanksgiving. 🙏 💙 🦃,

clean_body: To unsubscribe, | | Hi friend, I’m grateful for so many things this year. Time spent with family, friends, and neighbors. Working with our diverse communities, united by our shared love for Southwest Ohio. And for people like you, who haven’t given up on good governance and are willing to step up and fight for it. It’s been a rough year filled with uncertainty, but this past month has felt like finding our way back to steady ground. You’re the engine powering our vision forward: one where no one, including the president, is above the law, and where families can rest easy after a hard day’s work, knowing they can afford to care for their loved ones. I’m honored to have earned the trust of voters once more and to represent OH-01 in Washington. And I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work. But for today, I’m celebrating the renewed hope and determination you give me as we push for a better future for Southwest Ohio kids and families. From our family to yours, Happy Thanksgiving. 🙏 💙 🦃, Greg Landsman = | | Paid for by Landsman for Congress P.O. Box 68033, Cincinnati, OH 45206 www.landsmanforcongress.com Please consider making a =.
